articles.title: Sechs Modelle, vier Prozessoren: Welchen Mac brauche ich eigentlich?
articles.text:
Neo, Air, Pro, Mini, Studio, iMac: Welcher Mac ist der richtige für dich?
Als Steve Jobs 1996 zu Apple zurückkehrte, fand er ein Chaos an unterschiedlichen Computern vor. Er beschloss daraufhin, das Angebot stark zu vereinfachen. Ab August 1998 sollte es nur noch zwei Kategorien mit je zwei Geräten geben: Endnutzer:innen und Profis. Beide bräuchten je einen Mac für den Desktop und einen zum Mitnehmen. Das Konzept hielt sich lange. Wer unterwegs Office-Aufgaben erledigen wollte, wählte ein Macbook Air, für Videoschnitt ein Macbook Pro. Mittlerweile ist das nicht mehr ganz so einfach. Denn heutzutage will das Unternehmen doch wieder für jeden Anwendungsfall einen Mac im Angebot haben.
Aktuell hast du die Wahl zwischen sechs Produkten. Ob und wie sehr sie sich für Profis eignen, hängt dabei längst nicht mehr nur von der Kategorie, sondern auch von der Auswahl des eingebauten Prozessors ab. Hier ist das Angebot ebenfalls unübersichtlich. Denn ein A18 Pro eignet sich gar nicht für Profis und der M5 Ultra ist der aktuell leistungsstärkste Chip. Trotzdem gibt es aber schon einen M6. Wie sollte man also wählen?
Die aktuellen Mac-Modelle
Macbook Neo
Das Macbook Neo ist das günstigste, aber auch leistungsschwächste Modell, das Apple verkauft. Der enthaltende A18-Pro-Prozessor ist mitnichten ein Chip, mit dem sich das Unternehmen an Videocreator richtet. Stattdessen stammt er aus dem iPhone 16 Pro. Zusätzlich verbaut Apple in der Basisvariante acht Gigabyte Arbeits- und 256 Gigabyte SSD-Speicher. Den RAM kann man nicht aufrüsten, den SSD-Speicher gegen Aufpreis immerhin verdoppeln. Außerdem fehlen kleinere Funktionen wie der dynamische Weißabgleich Truetone oder aber der Fingerabdrucksensor Touch-ID in der Basis-Konfiguration. Interessant ist das Gerät vor allem für Schüler:innen, Student:innen oder Privatpersonen, die einen Mac wollen, ohne gleich über 1.000 Euro dafür zu bezahlen. Schul-, Uni- und Office-Arbeiten erledigt das Macbook Neo ohne Probleme.
iMac
Ähnlich ist der iMac gelagert – allerdings mit deutlich leistungsstärkerer Hardware. Aktuell liefert Apple den All-in-One-Computer mit einem M4-Chip, 16, 24 oder 32 Gigabyte Arbeitsspeicher und bis zwei Terabyte SSD-Speicher an. Je nach Konfiguration kann er vielseitig eingesetzt werden, etwa als Familien-Computer im Wohnzimmer, als Hauptgerät im Studentenleben oder aber in Agenturen zur Foto- und Videobearbeitung. Gegen Aufpreis verkauft Apple den iMac auch mit mattem Display, also mit dem sogenannten Nanotextur-Glas. Das ist ansonsten nur Profi-Geräten vorbehalten. Ob es derzeit eine gute Idee ist, den iMac zu kaufen, ist schwer einzuschätzen. Die aktuelle Variante hatte im Herbst 2024 in den Verkauf gebracht. Gut möglich, dass in wenigen Wochen eine Auffrischung mit M6-Prozessor folgt.
Mac Mini
Eine Alternative zum iMac ist der Mac Mini, den Apple noch (knapp) unter 1.000 Euro verkauft. Der kleine stationäre Rechner kommt ab sofort mit dem M6-Prozessor, ist also schon auf dem aktuellsten Level unterwegs. Der kleinste Mac ist ebenso vielseitig einsetzbar – als Familien-Computer, als Server für KI-Agenten wie Openclaw oder Hermes, als Desktop-Workstation für Entwickler:innen oder Kreative. Für Letztere eignet sich vor allem die teurere Variante mit dem M5-Pro-Prozessor.
Mac Studio
Apples aktuell schnellster Desktop-Computer hat den Mac Pro mittlerweile vollständig ersetzt. Entsprechend ist der Mac Studio mit den stärksten Chips ausgestattet. Sowohl der M5 Max als auch der M5 Ultra sollen sich für die Berechnung komplexer Modelle eignen, die Bearbeitung sehr großer Videodateien ermöglichen oder dafür sorgen, dass lokale KI-Modelle problemlos laufen. Daraus wird schon klar: Dieser Computer eignet sich vor allem für Profis.
Macbook Air
Das Macbook Air bleibt dank starker Akkulaufzeit der “Go to”-Laptop für alle, die möglichst mobil arbeiten wollen. Es ist der derzeit flachste Computer, den Apple verkauft. In der kleineren 13-Zoll-Variante wiegt das Air nur 1,2 Kilogramm. Wofür man es gebrauchen kann, hängt ebenfalls stark von der Ausstattung ab. Videoschnitt ist möglich, allerdings wäre hier ein Aufschlag zum verbauten M5 mit je zehn Rechen- und Grafikkernen ratsam. In der Basis-Version fehlen dem Chip zwei Grafikkerne. Der Speicher lässt sich auf Wunsch auf bis zu vier Terabyte aufrüsten. Das kostet allerdings auch bis zu 1.650 Euro und damit mehr als der Mac selbst in der Grundform.
Macbook Pro
Das Macbook Pro ist das Powerhouse für unterwegs und eignet sich nicht nur für Foto- und Videobearbeitung, sondern auch für komplexe 3D-Modellierungen oder ähnlich gelagerte anspruchsvolle Aufgaben. Hier kommt es ebenfalls auf den Prozessor an. Man bekommt das Profi-Gerät wahlweise mit M5, M5 Pro oder M5 Max, dem derzeit stärksten Mobilprozessor aus Cupertino. Außerdem setzt Apple hier auf eine Mini-LED-Hintergrundbeleuchtung – auf Wunsch und gegen Aufpreis gibt es dies ebenfalls mit Nanotextur-Glas. Die Leistung hat allerdings ihren Preis. Ein voll ausgestattetes Macbook Pro kostet über 11.000 Euro. In der 16-Zoll-Variante sogar noch etwas mehr.
Chipkunde: M4 vs. M5 vs. M6
Wie beschrieben, ist der Chip entscheidend für die gebotene Leistung. Neuere Ausgaben sind in der Regel etwas schneller als die jeweiligen Vorgänger. Zudem bietet Apple die Prozessoren oft auch ohne Pro-, Max- oder Ultra-Zusatz in mehreren Konfigurationen an. Dann unterscheiden sie sich vor allem bei der Anzahl der Grafikkerne. Wichtig ist das für Kreative wie Grafikdesigner:innen. Ebenfalls wichtig:
Je weiter oben der Chip angesiedelt ist, desto mehr gemeinsamen Speicher (Unified Memory) unterstützt er. Diesen teilt das System zwischen Prozessor, Neural Engine und Grafikeinheit auf. Je höher die Zahl, desto besser laufen auf dem Mac auch große lokale KI-Modelle. Die Spannbreite erstreckt sich aktuell vom M4-Prozessor mit maximal 32 Gigabyte hin zum M5 Ultra mit bis zu 512 Gigabyte Unified Memory.
Der M4 ist derzeit der dienstälteste Mac-Prozessor, den Apple neben dem iPad Air noch im iMac verkauft. Er stammt noch aus dem Jahr 2024 und ist im November zwei Jahre alt. Er trug seinen Teil dazu bei, dass Apple an der KI-Revolution teilhatte, denn der sparsame wie leistungsstarke Chip erwies sich im damals noch günstigen Mac Mini als ideale Lösung für agentische KI wie sie Openclaw erstmals für die breite Masse zugänglich machte. Infolge dessen war der Mac Mini mit einem Einstiegspreis von nur 699 Euro bei Technik-Fans extrem beliebt.
Hier will Apple mit dem M6 jetzt ansetzen. Laut Hersteller bietet der Chip, verglichen mit einem M4 mit je zehn CPU- und Grafikkernen und 32 Gigabyte Arbeitsspeicher, eine bis zu viermal schnellere Performance bei KI‑Anwendungen. Die Grafikleistung soll sich zudem verdoppelt und die CPU-Performance 40 Prozent zugenommen haben. Rund fünfmal schneller sollen lokale KI-Modelle in der App LM Studio Prompts verarbeiten. Heruntergebrochen heißt es das: Bei lokaler KI hat die Leistung stark zugenommen, die Grafikleistung hat sich (auch in Spielen) verbessert und alltägliche Aufgaben löst der M6 etwas schneller als der M4-Prozessor.
Der Mac Mini ist bislang allerdings der einzige Apple-Computer mit M6‑Prozessor. In Geräten wie dem Macbook Air ist der M5 verbaut. Diese gibt es seit Frühjahr 2026 zu kaufen. Hier gibt Apple ebenfalls an, die KI-Leistung verbessert zu haben. Wie beim M6-Chip spricht Apple von einer vierfachen Leistung bei KI-Tasks im Vergleich zum Vorgänger M4.
Der M5 Pro soll sich ebenfalls gut für lokale KI‑Modelle eignen. Apple hebt vor allem den gemeinsamen Speicher von bis zu 64 Gigabyte hervor, vergleicht die Kennzahlen allerdings nicht mit dem M4 sondern mit dem M4 Pro. Auch hier sollen Prompts in LM Studio nun viermal schneller verarbeitet werden. Im Vergleich zum Vorgänger fallen die weiteren Zahlen aber nicht ganz so beeindruckend aus. Etwas besseres Raytracing, etwas besser in der Bildbearbeitung als der M4 Pro.
Ähnlich sieht es bei den stärkeren Modellen Max und Ultra aus. Sie sollen Prompts knapp viermal so schnell verarbeiten wie die jeweiligen Vorgänger M3 Max und Ultra. Überdies eignen sich Mac Studios, die mit den beiden Chips ausgestattet sind, vor allem für Profi-Anwender:innen, etwa zur Entwicklung von Videostudiospielen oder zur Echtzeitarbeit mit 3D‑Material. Gründe, für “normale” Nutzer:innen, zu so einem Profigerät zu greifen, gibt es nicht.
Ich habe schon einen Mac: Muss ich wecheln?
Die Frage ist nun: Was bedeutet das für den Einzelnen? Apples Zahlen können verwirren, denn sie vergleichen die Leistung nicht immer mit den direkten Vorgängern, sondern oftmals auch mit der allerersten Generation der M-Chips, die je nach Modell 2020 oder 2021 gestartet ist. Grundsätzlich gilt: Die Sprünge zwischen den einzelnen Generationen sind nicht mehr so groß, wie beim Wechsel von Intel auf Apple Silicon. Ob du von einem älteren auf einen neueren Mac wechseln willst, hängt davon ab, was du damit vorhast.
Hast du etwa ein Macbook Air mit M2‑Prozessor und acht Gigabyte Arbeitsspeicher, interessiert dich aber mittlerweile für lokale KI? Dann lohnt sich ein Wechsel auf ein stärkeres Modell wie einen Mac Mini, am besten direkt mit mehr als 16 Gigabyte Arbeitsspeicher. Nutzt du das Gerät vor allem für Office-Aufgaben und bist mit der Geschwindigkeit und Akkulaufzeit noch zufrieden? Dann gibt es keinen Anlass für einen Wechsel. Zumal Apple die Preise vieler Modelle nach oben angepasst hat. Noch bekommen außerdem alle Modelle mit Apple Silicon Betriebssystem Updates, wie auf das neue macOS 27 Golden Gate. Sie sind zudem kompatibel mit Apples KI-Paket Apple Intelligence und bieten auch in der EU direkten Zugriff auf Siri AI, wenn du die Siri- und die Systemsprache auf US-Englisch umstellst.
Anders sieht der Fall aus, wenn du einen älteren Silicon-Mac hast und (perspektivisch) alle neuen Funktionen willst. Denn wie Apples Software-Chef Craig Federighi erklärte, bekommen nur sehr aktuelle Maschinen Zugriff auf die leistungsfähigsten On-Device-Modelle. Mac-Nutzer:innen brauchen hierfür mindestens ein Gerät mit M3 und zwölf Gigabyte Arbeitsspeicher.
Besitzt du noch einen Intel-Mac, kannst du ebenfalls stark von einem Wechsel profitieren. Denn mittlerweile erhalten diese Macs keine Betriebssystem-Updates mehr. Schon 2026 müssen sie passen. macOS 27 Golden Gate ist nur für Computer mit Apple Silicon verfügbar. Ursprünglich hatte Apple drei Jahre lang fortlaufende Sicherheitsupdates für Intel-Macs in Aussicht gestellt. Mittlerweile hat das Unternehmen die Angabe von der entsprechenden Supportseite aber entfernt. Eine sprichwörtliche Lücke hat die Sache aber ohnehin, wie unter anderem Heise berichtet. Demnach fixt Apple bei älteren Betriebssystemen nur wirklich kritische Fehler. Kleinere Bugs können ungepatcht bleiben. Im Detail erfährt man das nicht. Neben dem bestehenden Software-Support dürften sich Wechsler:innen aber auch über das gestiegene Arbeitstempo freuen.
Wer sparen will, sollte übrigens nicht direkt bei Apple nach neuer Hardware suchen. In der Regel bleibt die unverbindliche Preisempfehlung direkt beim Hersteller so lange bestehen, bis ein neues Produkt nachrückt. Angebote gibt es nicht. Das sieht im Handel anders aus. Bei diversen Online-Händlern bekommst du etwa das Macbook Neo trotz Preiserhöhung oft für 670 Euro. Das ist 30 Euro günstiger als Apples ursprüngliche Preisempfehlung und 130 Euro günstiger als der Preis, den Apple derzeit aufruft.
Fazit
15 Jahre nach dem Rücktritt von Steve Jobs ist das Mac-Ökosystem bei Apple wieder so unübersichtlich wie Mitte der 90er-Jahre. Neben etlichen Kategorien gibt es zudem mehrere Prozessoren, auf die du Rücksicht nehmen musst. Immerhin: Wenn du dich einmal entschieden hast und einen aktuellen Mac kaufst, hast du ein paar Jahre Ruhe damit. Vorher musst du dir aber klar werden, wofür du den Computer wirklich verwenden willst. Es muss nicht immer das schicke oder neue Pro sein. Für viele alltägliche Aufgaben reicht auch das Neo oder eine kleinere Konfiguration des Air.

articles.title: Reports of our death are greatly exaggerated, Rajendran Dandapani tells audience at DevSparks Chennai
articles.text:
Reports of our death are greatly exaggerated, Rajendran Dandapani tells audience at DevSparks Chennai
Zoho Corporation Director Rajendran Dandapani said AI may take over more of the work of writing code, but developers will increasingly need to focus on deciding what to build, directing AI systems, and judging what they produce.
For a developer, there is something unsettling about watching an AI agent write code. It might not be perfect, but it is often good enough to raise an uncomfortable question: if machines can increasingly do the work, what exactly is the developer supposed to do?
That was the question Rajendran Dandapani, Director at Zoho Corporation, posed to the audience at DevSparks Chennai in his opening session, titled ‘The Developer is Dead. Long Live the Developer’. Despite the ominous title, his argument was less about the disappearance of developers and more about the changing nature of their work.
“Reports of our death are greatly exaggerated,” Dandapani said, borrowing Steve Jobs’ famous line, which in turn was an adaptation of Mark Twain’s, to frame the discussion.
Every technology shift changes the job
The anxiety surrounding AI-assisted development, he suggested, is not entirely new. In 1957, when John Backus introduced FORTRAN and the compiler, programmers worried that machines would produce inefficient code and that people who did not understand the underlying hardware would be able to write software.
Dandapani pointed out that similar concerns are being echoed today. Developers argue that AI-generated code may be inefficient, consume costly tokens and allow people without traditional programming expertise to build software, a practice often called “vibecoding”.
“But technological efficiency does not always mean less work. Sometimes it makes a previously expensive activity cheap enough that far more people begin doing it,” he said.
Dandapani referred to the Jevons paradox, which describes how improvements in efficiency can actually increase consumption of a resource. More efficient steam engines, for instance, did not eliminate the use of coal. Similarly, making software easier to build could expand the number of people and organizations building it.
“We are not seeing fewer developers. We are seeing a plethora, a Cambrian explosion. Almost everyone wants to build an app now,” he said.
From writing code to deciding what should be built
Dandapani feels the bigger question is what happens when writing code stops being the main bottleneck.
He described this as another step in the evolution of the developer’s role. As AI becomes capable of producing software, developers may move from being primarily authors of code to becoming editors, directors, and judges of what machines create.
“If everything can be built today, you need not worry about how to build but what to build. That is the question,” he said.
That puts a premium on something AI does not automatically provide: taste. Dandapani used the idea of a “taste gap” to describe the distance between what someone creates and what they know to be good.
Developers traditionally build technical skill and judgement together, learning over years to distinguish good software from bad software. AI can disrupt that process by producing impressive results before the person using it has developed the judgement to properly evaluate them.
“The problem with AI is that it has given us awesomeness without giving us taste,” Dandapani said.
His prescription was to use the time saved by AI differently. If a developer can complete a task 10X faster, the additional time should not simply be spent generating 10X as much code. It should be spent understanding, judging and improving what AI has produced.
“If AI is doing your job 10X faster, spend nine-tenths of the time understanding, judging, editing, discerning, and discovering,” he said.
There is another consequence to this shift that companies will have to contend with. If AI takes over much of the work traditionally given to junior developers, organizations may hire fewer entry-level engineers today. But this could also weaken the pipeline that produces experienced developers tomorrow.
“The senior is the person who has struggled as a junior,” said Dandapani, pointing to the importance of learning through customers, company culture, and the specific problems an organization is trying to solve.
The developer, he assured the audience, may not be disappearing so much as moving up the stack. Less time could be spent translating instructions into code, and more time deciding what deserves to be built, directing AI systems and determining whether what they produce is worth shipping.
“The code may increasingly belong to the machine, but the judgement around it remains human,” Dandapani said before exiting the stage.
Edited by Teja Lele

articles.title: Bradé à moins de 1 000 €, ce laptop de 14" avec écran OLED et autonomie XL est fait pour travailler partout sans prise de tête — Frandroid
articles.text:
Si vous cherchez un PC portable pour vous accompagner au quotidien, nous vous proposons ce HP Omnibook de 14 pouces qui brille particulièrement par son écran OLED, son poids contenu et surtout par une autonomie qui lui permet de tenir facilement une journée sans forcer. C’est clairement un PC pour la bureautique, par contre il ne faut pas le choisir pour le gaming, le montage régulier de vidéos lourdes. En effet, il fonctionne sous Windows sur Arm, une architecture différente de x86 et x64, et si l’expérience s’est améliorée avec le temps, elle n’est pas au point partout. Il se retrouve en promo sur Boulanger pour 999,99 euros au lieu de 1 199 euros le temps de quelques jours.
Les atouts du HP Omnibook 14
- Un écran OLED de 14 pouces au format 16:10, très confortable
- Une autonomie supérieure à 20h en lecture vidéo
- 1,3 kg sur la balance et 1,26 cm d’épaisseur, un plaisir
Le HP Omnibook 14 est un PC portable qui coûte 1 199 euros de base, mais qui passe à 999,99 euros le temps d’une promo sur Boulanger.
Un ultraportable OLED endurant mais limité en jeu
Le HP Omnibook 5 14-he1003nfx mise sur sa dalle OLED de 14 pouces au format 16:10 avec une définition de 1 920 x 1 200 pixels pour une couverture annoncée de 95 % du DCI-P3. Si vous mettez l’accent sur le confort, c’est clairement un atout face à un LCD classique. De plus, la configuration est équilibrée pour les usages quotidiens avec un processeur Snapdragon X2 Plus, 16 Go de RAM LPDDR5x soudée et un SSD de 512 Go dans un châssis de 1,3 kg et 1,26 cm d’épaisseur.
L’autonomie est l’un des points les plus marquants de cette machine. La fiche technique annonce 20h en lecture vidéo, ce qui laisse supposer une journée d’utilisation facile en usage classique. Ainsi, si vous cherchez de quoi télétravailler tranquillement, c’est un bon candidat. C’est en partie dû à l’architecture Arm qui est moins énergivore, mais qui a une contrepartie contraignante : il faut vérifier la compatibilité de vos logiciels, pilotes et accessoires avec Arm avant de les acheter ou de les installer, sous peine de dysfonctionnements.
Une configuration moderne soignée
La connectique de ce HP Omnibook 14 est mesurée, avec deux ports USB-C 10 Gbit/s compatibles recharge et DisplayPort, un seul port USB-A et une prise jack, mais sans HDMI ni lecteur de carte. En revanche, vous disposez du Wi-Fi 7, le Bluetooth 6.0 et une webcam Full HD infrarouge compatible Windows Hello. La puce Snapdragon accélère localement certaines fonctions d’IA de Windows, ce qui renforce son efficacité énergétique.
On peut s’étonner de certains choix concernant l’équipement de cet ultraportable d’un certain standing, mine de rien. C’est le cas du clavier, qui n’est pas rétroéclairé selon la fiche, ou de l’absence de pavé numérique (ce qui s’explique par son format compact). Le câble de charge n’est pas fourni alors qu’un adaptateur 65 W est recommandé ; pour un laptop à 1 000 euros, on aurait aimé que ce soit le cas. De plus, la mémoire vive est soudée, ce qui limite fortement son évolutivité ou sa réparabilité. C’est donc un laptop à choisir si vous cherchez l’autonomie, la légèreté et l’agrément d’un écran OLED plutôt que la polyvalence ou la vocation créative.
Nous pouvons aussi vous recommander de lire notre guide comparatif sur les meilleurs ultraportables du moment, si vous cherchez un ultrabook pour vous accompagner au quotidien.

articles.title: South Africa’s Bank Zero breaks even as partnerships fuel growth
articles.text:
Bank Zero, the South African app-only bank, has reached break-even five years after opening to the public, with a partnership model that could now let it scale far beyond its own customer base.
The lender recorded its first break-even month in August, meaning its revenue covered its operating costs for the month. It does not mean the bank has become consistently profitable, and Bank Zero expects earnings to remain uneven in the short term.
Its next phase will rely on using its banking infrastructure to bring customers from fintechs, retailers, and digital platforms onto its platform. Bank Zero has 275,000 direct customers, while its alliance-banking partnerships are bringing another 500,000 customers onto the platform, although some overlap with its existing base.
The scale of the alliance-banking strategy marks a significant change for a bank originally designed to reach profitability with around 100,000 customers. Its challenge now is to show that the technology and cost structure that got it to break-even can support a much larger business.
Founded in 2018, Bank Zero opened to the public in August 2021 on the idea that a new lender did not need millions of customers to cover the cost of its technology and operations. Instead of buying an established banking platform and adapting it, the lender built its own.
“The cost profile is fundamentally different from a traditional bank – which is why break-even could be achieved at low customer numbers,” Yatin Narsai, Bank Zero’s chief executive officer (CEO), told TechCabal on Tuesday.
Bank Zero says it invested just under R300 million ($18.5 million) to build its banking platform, support systems and operate the bank until it reached break-even. Narsai estimates that buying and customising a comparable platform would have cost at least R3 billion ($184.6 million), before ongoing maintenance and modification costs.
The technology also gives Bank Zero control over features that would be difficult to add to an off-the-shelf system. Narsai claims a special patent makes card fraud and phishing impossible on the platform, while compliance controls are built directly into the system.
The bank’s model has also attracted more businesses than expected, with business customers now making up 18% of its customer base, compared with 10% in its original business case. More than 80% are registered companies.
“It’s not only about the zero fees. There is unique business-specific functionality,” Narsai said, pointing to digital mandates, multi-level authorisation chains, bulk payments and alerts when account details change.
The economics are also attractive to the bank. “Business customers are significantly more profitable than individuals due to higher account balances,” he added.
Alliance banking is where the model starts to look different. Instead of acquiring every customer itself, Bank Zero provides banking infrastructure to fintechs, retailers and digital platforms, allowing them to issue card products while bringing their customers, deposits and transaction activity onto the platform.
Bank Zero spent more than 18 months developing the alliance-banking proposition before going live in January 2026. Since then, Narsai says demand has been significant.
“Many scheme operators (businesses that run large payment schemes) are wanting to switch to a new end-to-end value chain that’s not only cheaper but also unique,” he stated.
Mukuru, an African remittance fintech serving migrant communities, shows what that could mean at scale. Narsai said 500,000 Mukuru customers are being onboarded onto Bank Zero’s platform, expanding the bank’s reach to more than 700,000 end account holders.
Chairman Michael Jordaan has described Bank Zero’s ability to reach profitability without a lending book as another advantage. The bank reached profitability with a relatively small customer base without taking on lending risk, with lending potentially providing another source of growth later.
Narsai is now focused on larger partnerships. “We’re going to focus on the big fish, and we are talking about big books,” he said.
Bank Zero originally expected to break even at around 100,000 customers. It reached that point with 275,000 customers, while its alliance-banking strategy is now pushing the platform towards a much larger customer base.
The lender expects earnings to remain uneven in the short term, but forecasts stronger revenue growth and healthy profit in 2027. Much of that growth is expected to come from alliance banking, with new foreign-exchange capabilities also awaiting approval from the South African Reserve Bank.
True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution. articles.title: Les Googlebooks débarquent : les 7 détails qui font des nouveaux PC Google des machines pas comme les autres
articles.text:
Après une annonce sur scène lors de sa Google I/O, la firme de Mountain View lance enfin son nouveau système d’exploitation pour ordinateurs portables, Googlebook. Ceux-ci n’ont pas vocation à remplacer les Chromebook, qui continueront d’exister sur le segment entré de gamme. Le but est plutôt de proposer une expérience plus raffinée et plus haut de gamme, avec un prix de départ fixé à 899 euros.
Pour l’occasion, Google s’est associé à cinq constructeurs de PC bien installés. Si nous vous détaillons les modèles dans un article dédié, nous allons ici tenter de vous décrire les sept détails qui démontrent que Google vise une approche nouvelle du PC avec ses Googlebook. 01net a pu assister à un ensemble de démonstration lors d’une table ronde en ligne, dont voici les points saillants.
Une base Android pour séduire les utilisateurs déjà conquis
Le premier point qu’il faut souligner avec ce lancement, c’est la proximité entre les Googlebooks et Android sur les Google Pixel. La firme californienne reprend tout le langage de design que l’on connaît déjà, jusqu’à imiter le menu des raccourcis rapides qu’on trouve en haut de l’écran d’un téléphone, pour le placer en haut à droite.
Mais c’est n’est pas tout. Vu que Googlebook est basé sur un fusion entre Android et ChromeOS, toutes les applications déjà disponibles sur le Play Store sont compatibles théoriquement. Google a même pris le temps de créer des étiquettes qui permettent de savoir si l’app est faite pour PC, smartphones, voire s’il s’agit d’une app compagnon à utiliser en parallèle d’un service sur le web.
De ce que nous avons vu, les apps prévues pour smartphones s’ouvriront dans une fenêtre flottante qu’il sera ensuite possible de redimensionner et avec laquelle vous pourrez interagir. Il est aussi possible d’afficher les apps de son smartphone Android en streaming sur le PC et d’interagir avec grâce à la souris. Certains ont déjà été optimisés pour le grand écran.
Une liste d’apps native a été partagée :
- Adobe Photoshop ;
- Adobe Lightroom ;
- CapCut ;
- Netflix ;
- Disney+.
10 ans de mises à jour
En débarquant, les Googlebooks amènent avec eux certaines des bonnes habitudes du smartphone. Google est un des premiers constructeurs à avoir promis 7 ans de mises à jour sur ses smartphones. Dans le monde des PC, il est rarissime qu’un constructeur avance le nombre d’années de suivi. Google a donc décidé d’importer cette bonne habitude dans ce secteur en promettant 10 années de mises à jour sur ses Googlebooks.
Magic Pointer
La souris du Googlebook n’est pas exactement la même que sur votre bon vieux PC Windows ou votre Mac. Google l’appelle Magic Pointer.
En secourant rapidement le curseur, ou via un raccourci clavier, le pointeur magique s’active. Concrètement, le pointeur va invoquer Gemini pour analyser du texte, des images, voire un contexte général pour vous apporter une aide.
Voici quelques exemples :
- Planification instantanée : sélectionnez un programme d’entraînement complexe pour un marathon sur une page Web, puis demandez à Gemini de cartographier automatiquement ces courses et de les planifier dans Google Agenda.
- Garantie : passez la souris sur un e-mail suspect et demandez à Gemini d’analyser le texte et les images pour vérifier s’il s’agit d’un spam ou d’un message légitime.
- Combinaison d’éléments visuels : sélectionnez un ensemble d’images avec Magic Pointer et demandez à Gemini de les visualiser ensemble. Pas de téléchargement, pas de chargement, pas de demande. Il suffit de pointer, de demander, et le résultat s’affiche.
Google prend, comme d’habitude, grand soin de rassurer ses utilisateurs sur les questions de vie privée. La firme de Mountain View précise que le Magic Pointer “s’éveille uniquement lorsqu’il est appelé, et reste inactif lorsqu’on ne l’utilise pas”.
Rambler
Vous retrouverez également Rambler, une fonctionnalité phare des derniers Pixel 11 Pro. Il s’agit d’une dictée vocale dopée à l’IA. Elle n’est pas exemple, capable de comprendre et d’ajuster le texte lorsque vous revenez en arrière ce que vous avez dit, ou encore de supprimer vos hésitations.
Créer son propre widget
Il va être possible de créer ses propres widgets, une fois encore, à l’instar du Pixel 11 sorti récemment. L’opération se passera via un simple chatbot auquel vous pourrez décrire ce dont vous avez besoin. Il sera possible d’itérer et de l’ajuster jusqu’à obtenir ce que vous souhaitez. Plutôt pratique.
Glow Bar
Tous les Googlebooks partageront un point commun au niveau de leur conception, une sorte de signature pour signaler qu’il s’agit d’un PC Google. Cela s’appelle la Glow Bar.
Il s’agit d’une bande LED située sur le capot arrière du PC. Là encore, les amateurs-rices de smartphone ne seront pas dépaysé-e-s, puisqu’on pense immédiatement à Hilight, le petit rond coloré ajouté au dos de l’iPhone 11.
Pour le moment, celle-ci semble intégrer des fonctionnalités assez simples, comme d’indiquer le niveau de batterie restant, mais l’API sera accessible aux développeurs tiers. Google compte ainsi sur ses partenaires pour s’emparer de cet accessoire. Pas sûr que cela aboutisse, à moins d’un énorme boom des Googlebook sur le marché des PC.
12 mois de Google AI Pro 5To offerts et un an de Nvidia GeForce Now
Pour terminer, tous les Googlebooks profiteront de deux périodes d’abonnement gratuit. D’abord 3 mois de YouTube Premium offert, ce qui permet de supprimer les pubs sur la plateforme rouge, de télécharger ses vidéos, de lire une vidéo avec l’écran éteint et d’écouter de la musique sur YouTube Music.
Deuxième service, et ce coup-ci en provenance d’un tiers : Nvidia s’associe à l’initiative de Google en offrant un an d’abonnement à GeForce Now, son service de jeux en cloud gaming. De quoi concurrencer légèrement Microsoft et son Xbox Game Pass qui profite aussi d’une offre sur la plupart des PC Windows.

articles.text:
Amazon French Week 2026 : voici les codes promos Prime exclusifs et comment en profiter
Pour marquer le lancement de sa French Week, Amazon déploie des remises immédiates allant jusqu'à 15 €. Mais attention, ces bons de réduction sont strictement réservés aux membres Prime et obéissent à des règles très précises. Voici comment optimiser votre panier.
Le coup d'envoi est donné ! Du 22 au 28 septembre, Amazon lance une semaine de réductions sur l'ensemble de son catalogue. Mais la véritable plus-value de cet événement réside dans les avantages exclusifs accordés aux abonnés Prime. En plus des milliers de ventes flash, l'e-commerçant américain propose deux codes promo pour baisser encore un peu la facture. Entre les différents paliers et les restrictions d'usage, il faut choisir la bonne stratégie avant de passer à la caisse.
Les codes promos Prime à retenir pour la French Week
La mécanique est pensée pour récompenser les membres Amazon Prime, avec deux niveaux de remise directe qui s'activent en fonction du montant total de votre commande :
- Le code FRPRIME5 offre 5 € de réduction immédiate dès 50 € d'achats éligibles.
- Le code FRPRIME15 permet de déduire 15 € dès 100 € d'achats éligibles.
Attention : des offres non cumulables (un seul choix possible)
C'est le point de vigilance majeur de cette édition 2026, et il est crucial pour ne pas gaspiller votre avantage. Les codes de la French Week ne sont pas cumulables. Plus important encore : chaque client Prime ne peut utiliser qu'un seul de ces deux codes pendant toute la durée de l'opération.
Concrètement, si vous utilisez le code de 5 € sur un premier achat, vous ne pourrez plus utiliser le code de 15 € sur une commande ultérieure, même si celle-ci dépasse les 100 €. Il est donc fortement conseillé de regrouper vos achats en une seule commande pour viser le palier des 100 € et maximiser la remise avec le code FRPRIME15.
Comment valider correctement votre remise immédiate
Pour que l'économie s'applique sans accroc, quelques étapes techniques sont à respecter. Le code (FRPRIME5 ou FRPRIME15) doit être saisi manuellement dans le champ "Vos cartes cadeaux et bons de réduction" lors de l'étape finale du paiement.
Un détail technique fondamental : l'option "Achat en 1-Click" court-circuite le tunnel de validation et ne permet pas d'appliquer ces codes promotionnels. Il faut donc impérativement ajouter vos articles au panier et suivre le parcours de commande classique pour que la déduction de 5 € ou 15 € soit bien prise en compte avant le paiement final.

articles.title: Final Fantasy VII Revelation pourra monter vos personnages de niveau automatiquement
articles.text:
Vous vous souvenez quand il fallait galérer plusieurs heures pour faire monter ses personnages de niveau dans les Final Fantasy de l’ère PlayStation ? Entre deux morceaux d’histoire, on prenait le temps, beaucoup de temps, pour aller battre le même ennemi pendant des heures afin de monter péniblement de niveau et devenir des sacs à PV invincibles.
Une époque qui semble désormais révolue, puisque Square Enix a confirmé qu’une option serait disponible à la sortie de Final Fantasy VII Revelation afin de faire monter automatiquement le niveau des personnages.
Le compte X de Genki relaie, ce 21 septembre 2026, une nouvelle interview accordée par Naoki Hamaguchi, réalisateur de la trilogie remake, à IGN Japan le 19 septembre 2026. Selon le développeur, les premiers retours des joueuses et des joueurs sur Final Fantasy VII Rebirth montrent que beaucoup souhaitaient en effet se concentrer sur la trame principale du jeu, sans forcément consacrer du temps aux nombreuses activités secondaires. Et quand on sait que le contenu annexe représentait une source importante d’expérience, celles et ceux qui passent à côté sont forcément désavantagés lorsqu’il s’agit de faire progresser leurs personnages.
À certains moments du jeu, Final Fantasy VII Revelation proposera donc une option permettant d’augmenter automatiquement le niveau des personnages jusqu’au niveau recommandé pour la suite de l’aventure. Plutôt que de retourner explorer le monde ou d’enchaîner les combats pour récupérer de l’expérience, les joueuses et les joueurs pourront se mettre directement au bon niveau et poursuivre l’histoire principale.
Il n’y aura plus besoin de faire du grinding dans Final Fantasy VII Revelation
Cette fonctionnalité, qui peut ressembler à de la triche, doit permettre de profiter de l’épisode ultime, Revelation, comme d’une aventure plus linéaire. Rassurez-vous, celles et ceux qui apprécient l’exploration et les quêtes secondaires pourront continuer à progresser de manière traditionnelle et chronophage.
Ce système ne semble donc pas destiné à remplacer complètement la progression classique d’un JRPG. Il s’agit plutôt d’une option pour les joueuses et les joueurs qui ne veulent pas faire tout le contenu secondaire, et veulent surtout éviter de gros pics de difficulté. Ce n’est d’ailleurs pas la première fois que Square Enix implémente des options facilitant la progression. Lors de la sortie de Final Fantasy VII Remake sur Switch 2 et Xbox Series, le studio avait notamment ajouté un mode permettant de conserver en permanence les PV et les PM au maximum, tout en infligeant 9 999 points de dégâts (le maximum du jeu) à chaque coup.
Faire des combats pour faire des combats semble donc être un passe-temps dont on peut désormais se passer. Tant que cette option reste facultative, pourquoi pas ? Parfois, ce n’est pas une mauvaise chose de simplement profiter d’une histoire et aller à l’essentiel, sans passer plusieurs heures à refaire les mêmes combats. Final Fantasy VII Revelation sortira le 8 avril 2027 sur PS5, Xbox Series X|S, Nintendo Switch 2 et PC.

articles.title: ¿Quieres invertir en criptomonedas? Conoce su valor y cómo ha fluctuado en las últimas horas
articles.text:
Las criptomonedas son un activo digital innovador que han experimentado un crecimiento monumental en los últimos tiempos debido a varios elementos que contribuyen a ello, entre ellos que algunos gobiernos hayan decidido darles una oportunidad como moneda de curso legal; no obstante, también han sufrido descalabros que han puesto en duda su viabilidad, como el más reciente episodio conocido como el "criptoinvierno".
Pese a este panorama, cada vez más personas han empezado a adquirir criptomonedas para poder invertir en algo "seguro" y "fiable" tanto a corto como a largo plazo, a pesar de los niveles extremos de inestabilidad que sufre constantemente.
PUBLICIDAD
Sin embargo, invertir o comprar en criptodivisas es más fácil de lo que parece. Hay que recordar que se trata de monedas virtuales, por lo que serán controladas en carteras o monederos que comparten esa particularidad, pues a diferencia del dinero corriente, no tienen un soporte físico.
El precio de las criptomonedas hoy
Esta es la cotización de las criptodivisas más destacadas en este momento.
El Bitcoin, cotiza a 81.594,61 dólares, lo que implicó un cambio de 0,557% en las últimas horas.
La segunda criptomoneda más popular del mercado, Ethereum, ha mostrado un movimiento de 0,568% en las últimas 24 horas, por lo que su valor se ubica en 2.658 dólares.
PUBLICIDAD
En el caso de TetherUs, su precio es de 1 dólares, por lo que en el último día tuvo un movimiento de 0,02%.
Por su parte, BNB, tiene un valor de 772,56 dólares, con un cambio de 1,38%, en cambio el Litecoin cotizó a 58.373 dólares, tras una variación de 0.06985734.
Finalmente, el Dogecoin, una de las monedas virtuales que fue impulsada por Elon Musk, tiene un valor de 0,09 dólares tras presentar un cambio de 1,73% en las últimas 24 horas.
Qué pasa con las criptodivisas
Luego de que en las primeras semanas de mayo del 2022 se viviera el "criptocrash" o "criptoinvierno" que dejaron al descubierto la enorme volatilidad de estas monedas digitales, ha llegado un nuevo periodo de relativa estabilidad.
PUBLICIDAD
Bitcoin, ethereum y BNB han mostrado variaciones "controladas", puesto que no se han disparado los precios como en semanas previas. Por ejemplo, a inicios de agosto, las mencionadas anteriormente tuvieron un cambio menor del 2%.
Por otra parte, algo que esta llamando la atención en el mundo de las criptomonedas es que China está ablandando sus restricciones y podría comenzar a permitir su uso. Específicamente sería Hong Kong en donde este cambio se haría presente.
Sumado a ello, la plataforma de transacciones digitales PayPal anunció su propia stablecoin llamada PayPal USD (PYUSD), que cuenta por el respaldo de depósitos en dólares, bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos a corto plazo y activos equivalentes.
PUBLICIDAD
La compañía ha afirmado en su declaración que permitirá la transferencia de fondos a monederos digitales de terceros y proporcionará detalles sobre cómo integrar su servicio en exchanges centralizados y descentralizados, con el objetivo de ser utilizado en Finanzas Descentralizadas (DeFi, por sus siglas en inglés). Por lo tanto, es muy probable que se utilice ampliamente en la industria Web3.
Criptomonedas en Latinoamérica
Criptomonedas en México: el Banco de México (Banxico) ha determinado que ninguna de las instituciones que participan en el sistema financiero nacional podrá hacer uso o deberá permitir operaciones de ninguna clase a través de este medio de pago.
En territorio mexicano el empresario Ricardo Salinas Pliego, uno de los más ricos del país, ha mostrado interés en las criptomonedas y ha asegurado que varios de sus negocios aceptarán bitcoin en el futuro, incluido su banco; hasta el momento una de sus tiendas más populares ya lo hace.
PUBLICIDAD
Criptomonedas en Perú: el Banco Central de Reserva del Perú (BCR) ha dejado en claro que su misión no es ser el primero ni el segundo banco central que regule el uso de las criptomonedas, ello debido a la inestabilidad que las caracteriza. Sin embargo, hace días el presidente del (BCR) aseguró que el BCR trabajaba en un proyecto de moneda digital propia.
Criptomonedas en Colombia: en la nación sudamericana hay más de 500 sitios donde es permitido pagar con criptodivisas. Colombia ocupa el puesto 14 entre 26 países de adopción de criptomonedas, según el informe de Finder.
PUBLICIDAD
Criptomonedas en Centroamérica: en el gobierno de El Salvador, el bitcoin, que en septiembre de 2021 se convirtió en moneda de curso legal, ha perdido oficialmente este estatus en este enero del 2025 tras una reforma aprobada por la Asamblea Legislativa del país. Según informó la prensa local, la modificación de la Ley Bitcoin fue impulsada por el gobierno del presidente Nayib Bukele y respaldada por la mayoría oficialista en el órgano legislativo. Este cambio marca el fin de una política que había colocado al país centroamericano en el centro del debate global sobre las criptomonedas.
¿Cómo crear una criptomoneda?
Al momento de crear una criptomoneda es importante primero determinar qué se desea tener: una moneda o un token. La primera usa su propia blockchain, mientras que la segunda se basa en una red preexistente.
PUBLICIDAD
De acuerdo con el sitio de Binance, para crear una criptomoneda se necesita de un gran equipo de desarrolladores y expertos; mientras que para el token sí se requieren conocimientos técnicos pero es posible crearlo en minutos a través del uso de otras blockchains como Ethereum o BNB, que son las más populares.
Los costos de creación, el tiempo requerido y el uso de fuerza de trabajo dependerá de si se opta por hacer una moneda virtual o un token. En éste último caso también se puede usar un código establecido para crear tokens o pagar para usar un servicio de creación de monedas.
PUBLICIDAD
Es importante saber que antes de crear una criptomoneda se debe considerar su utilidad y estado legal.
En el caso de elegir crear una criptomoneda, entonces se debe elegir una blockchain, posteriormente se debe hacer un plan acorde al funcionamiento y la funcionalidad de la blockchain para diseñar los nodos y la interfaz.

articles.text:
É oficial: Google lança os primeiros Googlebooks
Google iniciou pré-venda dos laptops da categoria Googlebook. Eles são produzidos por marcas como Acer, Asus, Dell, HP e Lenovo.
Os Googlebooks são oficiais. O Google começou a semana com o anúncio da pré-venda da nova categoria de laptops, que combina tecnologias do Android com recursos do ChromeOS. Ao contrário do que o nome sugere, os novos equipamentos não são fabricados pelo Google, mas por marcas como Acer, Asus, Dell, HP e Lenovo. Os preços começam em US$ 899 (R$ 4.594 na conversão direta).
O Google anunciou a categoria Googlebook em maio, durante o evento The Android Show: I/O Edition 2026. Na ocasião, a companhia deixou claro que a novidade teria como foco a execução de atividades via inteligência artificial. E continua sendo assim. As principais funcionalidades da categoria incluem:
Ao contrário da família Chromebook, que prioriza modelos de custo baixo a médio, a categoria Googlebook exige hardware avançado para dar conta das aplicações da IA, o que explica seus preços mais elevados.
Os modelos que estão chegando ao mercado contam com processadores Intel e Qualcomm que oferecem NPU de 45 TOPS ou mais, além de pelo menos 16 GB de RAM de alto desempenho (LPDDR5X), para você ter ideia.
Além disso, esses equipamentos precisam oferecer SSD com pelo menos 256 GB de capacidade, tela de alta resolução sensível a toques e bateria com autonomia de, no mínimo, 14 horas.
Para completar, o acabamento deve incluir características como teclado retroiluminado, trackpad com superfície de vidro e, como atributo mais notável, a Glowbar, uma barra de LED posicionada na tampa do notebook que dá sinais sobre inicialização, nível de carga de bateria, interações com o Gemini, entre outros.
No aspecto do software, os Googlebooks são capazes de executar aplicativos do Android, muitos dos quais são otimizados para uso via mouse/trackpad. Eles também saem de fábrica com ferramentas nativas do Google, a exemplo do Chrome, e contam com versões otimizadas de outros apps, como Adobe Photoshop e CapCut.
O Googlebook OS, como o sistema operacional da categoria é chamado, receberá atualizações funcionais e de segurança por até dez anos, de acordo com o Google.
A linha Googlebook entrou em pré-venda nos Estados Unidos. A primeira leva tem preços entre US$ 899 e US$ 1.299, como mostra a seguinte tabela:
| Modelo | Chip | Tela | RAM / SSD | Preço | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Acer Googlebook 14 | Intel Core Ultra 5 | 14″, OLED, 2,8K | 16 GB / 512 GB | US$ 899 | 
| Dell XPS Googlebook | Qualcomm Snapdragon X Elite | 13,4″, LCD, 2,5K | 16 GB / 512 GB | US$ 999 | 
| HP Googlebook 14 | Qualcomm Snapdragon X Elite | 14″, OLED, 2,8K | 16 GB / 512 GB | US$ 1.299 | 
| Asus Googlebook 14 | Intel Core Ultra 5 | 14″, OLED, 2,8K | 16 GB / 512 GB | US$ 1.299 | 
| Lenovo Googlebook 15 | Intel Core Ultra 5 | 15,3″, OLED, 2,8K | 16 GB / 512 GB | US$ 1.099 | 
O Google oferece, na compra de qualquer modelo, 12 meses de assinatura do Google AI Pro.
A pré-venda teve início hoje, mas as vendas oficiais estão previstas para 4 de outubro nos Estados Unidos por meio de canais como Google Store e Best Buy.
Você já deve ter imaginado, mas não custa reforçar: ainda não há previsão de venda oficial da linha Googlebook no Brasil.

articles.title: This one-command trick can put your localhost on the internet, no port forwarding required
articles.text:
In a nutshell: Sharing a dev project running on your own machine with someone on the other side of the internet has always been a small ordeal: deploy it somewhere, wrestle with port forwarding, or talk a client through a VPN. There's a free Cloudflare one-command fix for this however that just went viral among developers... five years after it shipped.
"Put localhost on the Internet," was the new pitch for an old feature that had Cloudflare at the top of Hacker News and X's dev circles for the last few days. The tool has existed since 2021, and let's you run one command: cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:8000, and whatever is running on your machine gets a public, encrypted address on trycloudflare.com.
No account, no DNS records, no poking holes in your router. When you kill the process, the URL dies with it. For anyone who has ever needed to show a client a half-finished build, the appeal is obvious. The rediscovery of the old tool drew variations of two reactions: people who had never heard of this and had a use for it that same day, and people who had been quietly using it for years and were baffled to see it treated as news.
 – Suganthan Mohanadasan (@suganthan) September 20, 2026
Cloudflare shipped Quick Tunnels in September 2021, built by a summer intern, and an account-free version existed even earlier under the old Argo Tunnel name. What changed this time is how the company marketed it again, with a new landing page that HN promptly dismantled as something that had apparently come out of a chatbot.
But regardless of this, we thought it was worth mentioning because many developers seemed genuinely surprised that this could solve a daily problem. Cloudflare, meanwhile, is repositioning the tool for the "agent era," complete with JSON output so a coding agent can read the generated URL. Developers in the thread wanted precisely that: a way to give a remote AI agent a reachable endpoint for something running on a machine at home.
 – onur ozcan (@oozn) September 20, 2026
The big catch is the same one that always applied. That URL is public and bots tend to find it fast. Security firms have spent two years documenting criminals abusing the free, anonymous version to stage malware. ngrok's founder, who invented this category, turned up in the thread to say his company killed anonymous tunnels years ago because the abuse wasn't worth it. But granted, treated as a temporary solution for a temporary problem, it should do the trick.

articles.title: Apple M6 Mac mini review: $300 price hike spoils a nice upgrade
articles.text:
These play-it-safe updates aren’t very exciting, but they’re also usually all upside—you get a year or two’s worth of technological improvements for the same price you would have paid for the older version yesterday. Unfortunately, 2026’s unprecedented memory crunch has upended that standard operating procedure.
The new Mac mini starts at $899 for a version with 16GB of RAM and 256GB of storage, a $300 increase for the same memory and storage specs you could get in the $599 M4 Mac mini in 2024.
The M4 Mac mini was a great general-purpose desktop computer and one of the best values Apple had ever offered in a desktop Mac. The M6 Mac mini is only one of those things. I’ll let you guess which.
Note that this review is specifically for the M6 version of the Mac mini. We didn’t get an M5 Pro Mac mini to review, but we’ll talk more about how its pricing and performance fits in for our Mac Studio review.
Design
The M4 Mac minis gave the computers their first full redesigns in nearly 15 years, so it’s not too surprising that the new Mac minis don’t change anything. Compared to the older Intel and M1/M2-era versions, they’re slightly taller (2 inches, up from 1.4), but they have a smaller 5×5-inch footprint (down from 7.7 inches squared). The system is actively cooled, with a fan vent on the bottom to make sure that whatever chip is inside can run at high sustained clock speeds (passively cooled Apple Silicon Macs like the MacBook Air have always been a bit slower than actively cooled Macs with the same chip).
All Mac minis have two 10 Gbps USB-C ports and a headphone jack on the front, and a 2.5 Gbps (default) or 10 Gbps (optional) Ethernet port and HDMI port on the back. Both also have three Thunderbolt ports on the back, but these are Thunderbolt 4 on the M6 Mac mini and Thunderbolt 5 on the M5 Pro version. That means the M6 mini’s ports top out at 40 Gbps, while the M5 Pro mini supports up to 120 Gbps speeds.
The Mac mini’s ports. No USB-A, but otherwise not bad for a system this small.
Credit:
Andrew Cunningham
The Mac mini’s ports. No USB-A, but otherwise not bad for a system this small.
Credit:
Andrew Cunningham
Realistically, there aren’t a ton of things on a Mac that can use all that bandwidth, especially since Apple doesn’t support external GPUs. But you do need a Thunderbolt 5 Mac to daisy-chain multiple computers together to form a compute cluster, so if that’s something you’re interested in, keep it in mind when you buy—maybe you’re buying multiple desktops, or maybe you already have an M5 Pro or M5 Max MacBook Pro you’d like to test the feature with.
The only real gripe with this design continues to be its bottom-rear-mounted power button; apparently, complaints about this are being sent to the same trash can Apple has always used for complaints about the Magic Mouse’s bottom-mounted charging port. It doesn’t come up often in everyday use if you just let your Mac go to sleep rather than shutting it down. But the positioning problem does really call attention to itself when you pair a TouchID-equipped external keyboard with the mini, since it requires a quick double-tap of the Mac’s power button before the sensor will work.
Meet the M6
Apple’s first M6-series chip is making its debut in the humble Mac mini, and the chip looks like the biggest upgrade Apple’s lower-end chip has gotten since the M4 generation added extra efficiency cores.
The headliner is the presence of two of Apple’s so-called “Super” cores, Apple’s nomenclature for P-cores that are even faster than its typical P-cores. Those are added on top of four P-cores and six E-cores for a total of 12 CPU cores. M4 and M5 both had 10 CPU cores. In the M4, these were split between four regular P-cores and six E-cores, whereas the M5 split them between four super cores and six E-cores (the M5’s cores were referred to as P-cores when it launched but were rebranded later when the M5 Pro and Max came out). The M1, M2, and M3 generations all used four P-cores and four E-cores.
The M6 has fewer super cores than the M5 but the same number of E-cores and four additional P-cores. While they’re apparently no longer “super,” the P-cores still perform well enough to ensure that the M6’s multi-core performance is better than M5’s overall.

Apple has mixed super cores with both other kinds of cores before, but this is its first chip to include all three kinds at once. To get around the awkwardness this might create at the CPU scheduler level, the built-in powermetrics tool suggests that Apple is still treating the M6 like a chip with just two types of cores. The six E-cores are all gathered together in one cluster, and the two Super cores and the four P-cores are all lumped together into a second six-core cluster called the “PS cluster.”
Powermetrics also reports that both the P- and S-cores have the same peak and minimum clock speeds, unlike in the M5 Pro and M5 Max where they’re different clusters with different clock speeds (both P- and S-cores in M6 range from 1.44 GHz to 4.79 GHz). The sysctl utility also suggests they share the same 20MB pool of L2 cache, up from 16MB for the 4-core Super cluster in the M5 (the E-core cluster has a bit more L2 cache, too, 8MB up from 6MB in the M5). The Super cores do have more L1 instruction and data cache, so they are definitely still different cores, and there are likely other differences that we can’t detect using software-level tools. But if you were wondering how macOS was going to treat a chip with three different kinds of CPU cores at a software level, the answer is “to act like it still has two different kinds of cores.”

The M6 gets additional GPU cores for the first time since the M2, increasing the count from 10 cores to 12. These cores include improved versions of the integrated neural accelerators Apple introduced in the M5-series GPU for speeding up AI and machine-learning workloads like ray-tracing and MetalFX upscaling. A “Dual 16-core Neural Engine” also bumps the number of Neural Engine cores from 16 to 32. Saying you have 2×16 of something strikes me as a roundabout way of saying you have 32 of something, but I suppose the end result is the same either way.
One small wrinkle in the M6 variants the Mac mini uses: The basic 16GB Mac mini offers 153 GB/s of memory bandwidth, the same amount as the M5. The 24GB and 32GB versions offer 170 GB/s, an 11 percent increase that should marginally improve graphics performance and the speed of any local AI models you run on this machine. Our review unit is the 24GB version.
What of the M6 Pro, M6 Max, or M6 Ultra? If the rumors are true, the M6 could end up being a lonely chip.
Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reports that Apple isn’t planning a full M6 chip generation and that it could skip directly to M7 branding for the Pro, Max, and Ultra chips. That would be a first for the company, which skipped shipping an M4 Ultra but has otherwise shipped a baseline, Pro, and Max-series chip in each generation so far.
But it makes sense for a couple of reasons. The first is that most of the M6’s gains can be attributed to its extra CPU and GPU cores relative to the M5, and the M5 Pro, M5 Max, and M5 Ultra all obviously still have more of both kinds of cores than the M6 does. The second is that it’s still pretty early for TSMC’s 2 nm process, following three generations where Apple used versions of TSMC’s 3 nm process, and Apple is probably fighting with every other fabless chipmaker on Earth to reserve capacity. Apple could be sticking with smaller, simpler 2 nm chips for now and saving its bigger and more complex chips for later, when capacity will be higher, yields will be better, and costs may be lower.
Performance
The new mini re-uses the launch strategy for last year’s Mac Studios, which used an M4 Max in the base model and an M3 Ultra in the top-tier configurations. The basic Mac mini uses the brand-new M6, while the semi-professional Mac mini tier gets the M5 Pro that we saw in MacBook Pros back in the spring.
This means the M6 mini has newer tech than the more-expensive M5 Pro mini—and marginally better single-core CPU performance, too. The M6’s single-core is roughly 8 to 10 percent faster than the M5 family’s in our benchmarks; graphics performance is also up by roughly 10 percent. In multi-core CPU benchmarks, the M6’s performance is roughly 20 percent faster than the M5.
But for heavy multi-core performance, having more cores is still more important than using the newest cores. The M5 Max (which uses the same 18-core CPU block as the M5 Pro, so it’s a decent stand-in) is still generally 60 or 70 percent faster than the M6 in our multi-core benchmarks.
If you’re comparing the last-generation mini to this one, the upgrades over the M4 are pretty substantial. Single-core CPU performance improves by between 20 and 30 percent in most tests, while both graphics performance and multi-core CPU performance are up by between 50 and 80 percent—and occasionally even more, in some tests. The M6 does nearly as well as the M4 Pro in the Blender benchmark and beats the M5 by around 40 percent, again suggesting that this benchmark in particular is benefiting from the GPU cores’ built-in Neural Accelerators.
Usually at this point we would talk about the chip’s estimated power consumption using the powermetrics tool, a built-in utility that gives clock speed and power consumption data for the CPU and GPU cores in Macs. This is a software-based reporting tool, which makes it imperfect for comparisons between chip generations. But it does at least give us some vague estimate of Apple’s power efficiency.
For the M6, powermetrics doesn’t actually report CPU power levels. It appears in the tool’s logs, but the value is always “0.” I’ve asked Apple whether this is a bug or an intentional behavior change (it still works fine for M5-generation chips), and I’ll update this if I get a response.
About that price
The $599 M4 Mac mini was a tiny, affordable desktop computer with as much speed and memory as most people need for general-purpose computing. You could quibble with the 256GB base storage, but it was still the most usable the basic Mac mini had ever been.
The M6 mini’s $899 starting price sets us way back. That’s a $300 increase in just under two years for a computer that has a faster chip in it but otherwise shares the key specs and most of the capabilities.
One could argue that this merely resets Mac mini pricing back to where it was circa 2020. A base M1 Mac mini cost $699 to start, and upgrading to 16GB of RAM added another $200. It just feels like a big step back, given how great the M4 mini was.
If you need a desktop computer right now for anything from basic browsing to less-intensive local AI models, this is still Apple’s most affordable computer (chatbots and image generation should run pretty well on it; more intensive coding-centric models will be a bit squeezed for RAM and memory bandwidth, even at 32GB). And even the $599 M4 mini was undercut by the kind of lowest-common-denominator cheap mini PCs you could get on Amazon. It’s just hard to swallow the current price, given how much better it was not all that long ago.
The good
An impressively fast and quiet little computer that can fill roles from “entry-level desktop” to “midrange coding and video editing rig.”
M6 is a big step up for Apple’s entry-level chip, with more CPU and GPU cores and other improvements.
Large improvements over the M4 mini, thanks to a two-generation silicon jump.
The bad
Zero upgradability, aside from what you can add with external accessories. What you buy is what you have until you buy the next thing.
256GB of storage in the base model is low, especially if you want to play games or run any kind of AI models locally.
Power button on the bottom is mildly inconvenient on the occasions you have to interact with it.
M6 version can’t be daisy-chained together with Thunderbolt 5 to join a compute cluster.
The ugly
The memory crisis means we can’t have nice things unless we’re willing to pay out the nose for them.
Andrew is a Senior Technology Reporter at Ars Technica, with a focus on consumer tech including computer hardware and in-depth reviews of operating systems like Windows and macOS. Andrew lives in Philadelphia and co-hosts a weekly book podcast called Overdue.

articles.title: Cloudflare saves 100 TB of RAM again, this time by slashing server hashes by 90% — cutting 100,000 entries down to 10,000 eliminates massive cache bloat
articles.text:
Cloudflare saves 100 TB of RAM again, this time by slashing server hashes by 90% — cutting 100,000 entries down to 10,000 eliminates massive cache bloat
A perfect illustration of an optimization for memory, after an optimization for speed
Cloudflare has saved 100 TB of RAM again, but this time by tuning its hash-mapping algorithm. One of Cloudflare's largest business use cases is data caching, more specifically serving a URL directly from memory or disk instead of fetching it from the live site, which may take a significant amount of time. The company uses its own open-source Pingora framework for the task of mapping an arbitrary URL to one of its cadre of cache servers, using the Ketama algorithm. This task is simple in concept, but can get quite tricky in an environment where it's expected that backend servers appear and disappear — and harder still when done at Cloudflare's scale.
"Backend routing," or the mapping of a URL to one of many cached servers, requires a lot of tables held in memory. An incoming URL is hashed (like you do with files with CRC-32), and that resulting number is taken and sent out to a server. The first instinct is to do this sequentially, one URL per server, but you hit the first problem: the same URLs aren't going to the same servers. So what you do is you make a hash corresponding to the server, say with its IP address and name, and match both hashes together by numerical proximity.
That sounds simple, and it works fine, as the URL hashes' distribution is going to be effectively random, and the requests will be redirected to the same server in an egalitarian way. But then you run face-first against the second problem: say you have four servers serving 25% of requests each, and #2 disappears because someone tripped on the power cable. You'll be forced to redirect the requests it handled onto whichever are closest in the hash map, and end up overloading server #3, the next one over, while #1 and #4 remain under little load.
The solution to that is to add more hashes per server and mix them up randomly. Now your four servers' many hashes have a random distribution, and if one dies, incoming requests should be equally distributed among the remaining ones. This takes a lot of memory, and it takes far more once you set up layers with weight rules (so that bigger servers handle more requests), and the fact that, due to content restrictions and architectural regions, not all servers can serve all requests. All told, Cloudflare was running with as many as 100,000 server hashes per machine, ballooning RAM requirements.
After judicious application of some algebra and basic statistics, Cloudflare engineers concluded that using those 100,000 hashes was far and away beyond the point of diminishing returns. The team calculated that a mere 10% of that amount was good enough for nearly the same results, as the error rate barely drops for each order of magnitude beyond 10,000. After some judicious wrangling of Rust's data structures to save 2 bytes per entry in the hash-server map. That sounds like nothing, but it quickly adds up with billions of records.
All things considered, the Cloudflare team saved around 100 TB of RAM total with this optimization. To play it safe, the team added this "v2" algorithm as a separate code path rather than replacing the code altogether — allowing them to simply swap back to the original one if something broke. Now if only all modern software were this judicious about resource usage.

Bruno Ferreira is a contributing writer for Tom's Hardware. He has decades of experience with PC hardware and assorted sundries, alongside a career as a developer. He's obsessed with detail and has a tendency to ramble on the topics he loves. When not doing that, he's usually playing games, or at live music shows and festivals.

Insta360 Link 2 Pro webcam: Two-minute review
Action camera brand Insta360 has been making a name for itself in the webcam space recently, breaking out with its first-ever webcam, the Link, back in 2022. Then we saw the Insta360 Link 2 in 2024, so while I was hoping for a Link 3 this year, instead we're getting an interstitial generation: say hello to the Insta360 Link 2 Pro.
I can't say I'm disappointed, mind you. The Link 2 was a fantastic webcam, and while the Link 2 Pro is a fairly straightforward hardware upgrade, I'm not one to complain about getting more of a good thing. The Pro model increases the price a bit, but also delivers improved internals: a bigger, better sensor and wider aperture for superior FOV and light balance mean that 4K video capture looks even prettier. It also adds a little gold trim around the lens.
Now, the Link 2 was already a pricey product, so there's no denying that the Insta360 Link 2 Pro is very expensive for a webcam, even a 4K-capable one. More on that further down in this review, but in short: want one of the best budget webcams? This ain't that.
But for professional users creating video content or making regular presentations over video conferencing, the Link 2 Pro should be a very serious consideration. It may not be cheap, but you get a lot of webcam for your money: the performance, design quality, and feature set are truly all best-in-class.
It's almost a bit surprising that more camera companies haven't made the jump to webcams. From old-guard industry titans like Canon to up-and-coming manufacturers like DJI, you'd imagine that more of them would want to capitalize on a product type that has only become more necessary in the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic and the rise of remote work.
But hey: their loss is Insta360's gain, having made a seamless jump from action-cams and drones to premium webcams. And make no mistake, the Link 2 Pro is indeed a premium piece of hardware.
The build quality on display here is nothing short of excellent. The casing is a pleasingly sturdy construction of matte plastic and metal, with a compact folding clip that snaps magnetically to the rotating gimbal mount, makning it easy to attach to any monitor. It also features an industry-standard threaded screwhole on the underside for fitting it to a tripod or arm mount.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Of course, the gimbal is arguably the star of the show here. A two-point mechanism that allows for both horizontal and vertical rotation of the main camera unit, the gimbal allows the camera to track your movements within a wide radius thanks to AI-powered head-tracking technology.
I tested this thoroughly, and it really works; even when I attempted to move completely out of frame, the camera was surprisingly adept at tracking my movements.
That's not all it's capable of, though. The gimbal also enables several of the Link 2 Pro's nifty presentation modes, including desktop mode (which points down to the surface in front of you, ideal for showing off physical documents), whiteboard mode (which frames and zooms on a whiteboard or similar presentation board), and the very clever 'pause-tracking' mode (which lets you designate a specific area where the tracking lingers naturally as it follows you around, creating a more dynamic feel to your footage).
It also doubles as a privacy feature (as opposed to a lens cover or camera killswitch), with the lens pointing directly down when not in use. A set of four 'recognition markers' is included in the box, which are used for some of the tracking-lock modes.
All this fancy functionality, as well as more 'conventional' features like light balance adjustment and digital zoom, is readily accessible through Insta360's free software. It's a solid tool that makes setting up your ideal video experience swift and seamless, but even better, it's also available as a phone app – perfect for quick adjustments without needing to fire up an extra piece of software on your PC while you're trying to record.
With all that fancy AI baked into the Link 2 Pro, you might be hoping for something a little more sophisticated than tracking modes. Worry not: like the previous Link 2, this webcam features a set of preloaded gesture controls, letting you control the camera with your hand movements rather than needing to adjust anything in the app.
These are fairly basic, but I found they worked well in practice. Holding up your palm freezes (or unfreezes) your tracking or auto-framing preset, holding up two fingers toggles the aforementioned whiteboard mode, and making an 'L' sign and moving your hand up and down lets you zoom in and out. It doesn't feel particularly natural at first, but I quickly found myself adapting to it.
Now, let's get to the meat of this review: how's that picture quality? Well, I'm very pleased to report that it's nothing short of excellent. Even in the poorly-lit, cramped little box of a room I call a home office, I don't think I've ever looked better on a monitor-mounted webcam.
4K footage is sharp and bright at 30FPS with solid color reproduction. The upgraded sensor and larger aperture compared to the previous model give the Link 2 Pro great performance across a range of light conditions, showing me clearly and well-illuminated whether it was the middle of the day with the curtains open or late at night by the light of my desk lamp.
The field of view is also reasonably wide at 83.9 degrees, making it easy to fit two or even three people in frame for presentations or podcasts. I've seen webcams with broader FOVs – in fact, I very recently reviewed the Razer Kiyo V2, which boasts an almost too-wide 91-degree FOV – but this is more or less perfect for mainstream use.
The built-in microphone array is pretty good considering that integrated microphones frequently feel like an afterthought on webcams. It offers clear enough audio capture with AI-powered background noise canceling for casual to intermediate users, great for stuff like Zoom meetings, but serious professional content creators will likely still want to invest in a proper standalone microphone.
In terms of flexibility of use, it's good, if not perfect. It's relatively compact, so while there are smaller and lighter webcams out there, you can still take it with you on the go if you work across multiple locations. If you fit it to a suitable mount, you can easily flip it onto its side to record vertical video for social media without any loss of functionality. The only issue is that it's a tad bulky to mount atop a laptop display unless your laptop has a particularly sturdy hinge, but that's a pretty minor issue in the grand scheme of things.
Overall, I'm finding very little I can criticize about the Insta360 Link 2 Pro. Other than the fact that it's undeniably expensive and will almost certainly be more than the average user actually needs, this is just a fundamentally great product that easily ranks among the best webcams on the market right now.
If I absolutely had to pick something to nitpick here, it might be that the Link 2 Pro lacks any kind of lens cap. Dust and debris getting stuck on or under the lens can be a real irritation with webcams, so it would have been a nice inclusion – especially considering that it's a pricey, high-end webcam. But that really is the definition of nitpicking; this is genuinely one of the greatest webcams I've seen in a long time.
Insta360 Link 2 Pro webcam: Price & availability
- How much does it cost? $249.99 / £239 / AU$439
- When is it available? Available now
- Where can you get it? The US, UK, and Australia
At $249.99 / £239 / AU$439, the Insta360 Link 2 Pro is the most expensive webcam the company offers, and it's undeniably a steep price for the average user. If you're purely looking for a high-quality 4K webcam and you're not bothered about fancy features, you could easily find one for half that price if you shop sales.
That being said, I'm not going to call this bad pricing. Considering that the Link 2 Pro is a high-end webcam aimed squarely at professionals who are serious about their hardware, along with the rich feature set and great picture quality it offers, I don't think the price is unreasonable – it's just not going to be worth it for more casual users.

articles.title: Marvel cancela 'Daredevil Born Again': la serie no volverá después de su tercera temporada
articles.text:
Disney ha puesto el último clavo en el ataúd de Daredevil: Born Again. La tercera temporada será la última de la serie, luego de que su showrunner, Dario Scardapane, dejara el proyecto en plena posproducción. La decisión forma parte de una reestructuración de Marvel Studios, en donde dejarán de invertir en series de televisión para enfocarse de nuevo en la pantalla grande.
De acuerdo con The Hollywood Reporter, Daredevil: Born Again llegará a su fin con la tercera temporada. A dos meses de que concluyera su rodaje, la serie basada en el popular superhéroe ya no continuará. Disney decidió no renovar el contrato de Scarpadane, quien tomó las riendas del proyecto luego de trabajar en The Punisher para Netflix.
Aunque Marvel Studios intentó enderezar el barco, la realidad es que la serie de Daredevil nunca consiguió repetir el éxito que obtuvo en Netflix. El proyecto tuvo un recorrido bastante accidentado desde su llegada a Disney+, comenzando con el plan inicial que se alejaba de la temática oscura y temas más maduros que hicieron famosa a la versión original. Las huelgas de 2023 fueron clave para que el estudio reiniciara el proyecto y se deshiciera de los guionistas originales, Matt Corman y Chris Ord, quienes apostaban por una serie más "light".
El cambio de rumbo también afectó al formato de la serie. Originalmente, la primera temporada tendría 18 episodios, pero tras el reinicio Marvel Studios redujo la cuota a 17 y los dividió en dos temporadas. La historia continuaría años después de los sucesos ocurridos en la serie de Netflix, con un Wilson Fisk tomando las riendas como alcalde de Nueva York y listo para vengarse de Matt Murdock y compañía.
La tercera temporada de Daredevil: Born Again será la última
La trama de la tercera temporada continúa con Fisk cargando contra todos los superhéroes que se cruzan en su camino. Si hacemos memoria, la segunda temporada cerró con el encarcelamiento de Daredevil, quien expuso su identidad secreta y ahora tendrá que lidiar con ello tras las rejas.
Aunque la próxima temporada será la última, el reparto promete un cierre por todo lo alto. Ya en los últimos capítulos habíamos visto al elenco de The Defenders con Krysten Ritter recuperando el papel de Jessica Jones y un cameo de Mike Colter como Luke Cage. Unas fotografías filtradas durante el rodaje de la tercera temporada mostraron a Finn Jones, quien regresa en su papel de Iron Fist para completar el grupo de superhéroes y enfrentar a un Kingpin ya despojado de su cargo como alcalde.
Se espera que la temporada final de Daredevil: Born Again se estrene en Disney+ en 2027, cerrando así un capítulo que comenzó hace más de una década en Netflix y que ha sobrevivido a cancelaciones, reinicios y cambios de guionistas antes de despedirse definitivamente.
Con el fin de sus series de televisión, Marvel centrará sus esfuerzos en la pantalla grande. El primer bombazo llegará con Avengers: Doomsday en diciembre de 2026 y un año más tarde repetirá la dosis con Avengers: Secret Wars. Otros proyectos que se encuentran en la lista son la película de Ghost Rider con Ryan Gosling y el esperado reboot de los X-Men, así como Black Panther 3.

articles.title: Meta's AI agent has been blocked from using Amazon.com | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Sunday night, users of Meta’s AI assistant Muse started getting a strange error message when they tried to buy goods on Amazon. As spotted by GeekWire, the error message read: “Continued access by an unauthorized AI agent violates Amazon’s Conditions of Use, to which our customers have agreed.”
In other words, Muse isn’t welcome as a shopper — and anyone trying to buy something on Amazon through the AI agent will have to find it somewhere else.
It’s easy to see the block as a tête-à-tête between tech giants. Amazon has its own cohort of foundation models, after all, along with one of the most popular inference platforms on the internet. As long as they’re under no legal obligation to open the doors to Muse, why would they?
But there are also substantive reasons Amazon might not want to be in the agentic commerce business just yet. If Muse makes a bad order, Amazon is going to be the one to clean it up — dealing with both the angry customer and the angry vendor. Muse has one of the lower hallucination rates, as AI models go, but it’s still pretty far from zero. Even if Amazon sees an opportunity in agent-driven commerce, they may want to wait a few more release cycles before rolling anything out.

The Investec Early Stage Entrepreneur of the Year Awards celebrate entrepreneurs building businesses with the potential to reshape industries across the future of professional services, enterprise software, consumer products, finance, health and wellness, deep tech, education and work, creativity, climate and female entrepreneurship.
