articles.title: Egypt’s Bekia raises $765k to scale recycling economy tech - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Egyptian startup Bekia, which is digitising waste collection, has raised a US$765,000 seed round to deepen its consumer app and launch its first B2B software product.
Founded in 2019, Bekia is a digital platform building the collection layer for Egypt’s recycling economy. The platform began with a consumer app – a household books a pickup, a collector arrives at a scheduled time, material is weighed on the spot at a published rate, and payment goes to a bank account or digital wallet.
At the end of October, Bekia will launch Bekia Next, which turns that data into verified CO₂-avoidance certificates for corporate clients using established international carbon accounting methodology. It is the first thing Bekia sells as a subscription rather than a service.
The startup’s US$765,000 funding round is led by Madica, the Africa-focused investment programme affiliated with Flourish Ventures, and also features Catalyst Fund and Dakar-based Jambaar Capital. Bekia will use the funding to grow its engineering team, take Bekia Next to market, and begin testing the model in a second African market.
“Egypt’s recycling sector has always worked — it just worked invisibly, on cash and trust, with no record of any of it,” said Alaa Afifi, founder and CEO of Bekia. “We built the software layer that changes that: a collector gets a transaction history, a factory gets traceable supply, a household learns what its waste is actually worth. The material itself is a commodity, but the record of it isn’t, and nobody in our market owns that record yet.”
“What excites us about Bekia is how the team is drawing on its firsthand understanding of waste collection in Egypt to build a more interconnected, tech-driven ecosystem serving households, small businesses and large industrial waste producers,” said Emmanuel Adegboye, head of Madica. “We’re proud to welcome them to the Madica programme and support that ambition with long-term capital, company-building expertise and networks.”

articles.title: Microsoft finally fixes this annoying Excel paste problem, but you probably never even noticed
articles.text:
Microsoft finally fixes this annoying Excel paste problem, but you probably never even noticed
Excel has been failing to paste for some users
- A recent update introduced a new bug affecting pasting in Excel
- Excel 2016 just got a hotfix, but Microsoft admits issues can persist
- Temporary workaround is available by selecting 'Paste Special'
Although a recent Microsoft Excel security update brought with it a highly annoying bug impacting copying and pasting functionalities across the spreadsheet software, it's already issued a partial fix.
Just days after the glitch was introduced with a September 8 2026 security update (KB5002914), the company has released a hot fix rather than forcing users to wait until the next cycle.
But this fix in particular only applies to Excel 2016, which is unlikely to have as much reach and global usage as Microsoft 365 versions of the app, therefore many users won't even have been aware of the issue.
Excel just got an important new fix
Other non-365 versions of Excel were also impacted. "In Microsoft Excel 2024, 2021, 2019, and 2016, as well as Excel Online in Office Online Server, the paste operation might fail silently," the company explained in a status update.
"Although users try to paste content, the source remains selected and the destination is unmodified," the update reads, confirming that users didn't receive an error message or sound to let them know of the failure.
Office LTSC 2021 and 2024 are officially fixed, Microsoft confirmed, but a only a mitigation is available for Office LTSC 2019 and Office 2016, so users may still experience some problems.
Thankfully, while a full fix is in the works, Microsoft offered up a pretty simple workaround. Pasting 'Special' from the Home tab is all it takes, with conditional formatting apparently causing headaches for now.

articles.title: Yoniq Portal : la console portable au look de manette PlayStation 2 sera à moins de 200 dollars
articles.text:
Un tarif qui ne semble pas complètement dingue, mais toujours peu d'informations techniques et pas non plus de date de sortie officielle.
La Yoniq Portal se précise enfin avec un tarif de lancement, mais la console portable inspirée de la fameuse manette de la PlayStation 2 signée Sony conserve encore une bonne partie de ses secrets.
Une console qui joue à fond la carte de la nostalgie
Déjà évoquée en août dernier, la console Yoniq Portal avait attiré l'attention par son design pour le moins original : la machine reprend effectivement les lignes caractéristiques de la mythique DualShock 2.
Présentée pour la première fois lors de la Gamescom 2026, la machine revient aujourd'hui sur le devant de la scène avec un prix annoncé à 199 dollars aux États-Unis, contre 219 dollars au tarif normal. En Europe, Yoniq affiche un prix de 172,99 euros, tandis que le Royaume-Uni bénéficiera d'un tarif de 148,99 livres. La marque n'a toutefois toujours pas communiqué de date de commercialisation précise.
La Portal reprend donc les principaux éléments de la manette de la PlayStation 2, avec une croix directionnelle, deux sticks analogiques, les quatre boutons de façade et les gâchettes. La principale différence tient évidemment à l'écran, installé au centre de l'appareil, entre les deux sticks. Sa diagonale serait de 4,5 pouces. Les visuels dévoilent également un port USB-C, une prise casque de 3,5 mm et un lecteur de cartes microSD. La console dispose par ailleurs d'un système de refroidissement actif, avec des ouvertures d'aération visibles sur la partie supérieure et à l'arrière.
Pour le reste, Yoniq reste – encore et toujours – particulièrement discret. Le fabricant n'a pas dévoilé le processeur, la quantité de mémoire vive, la capacité de stockage ou encore la définition exacte de l'écran et la capacité de la batterie. Un élément présenté comme un emplacement « Memory Card » apparaît sur certains rendus, sans que sa fonction soit expliquée. À ce stade, le prix permet donc de mieux situer la Portal, mais il reste impossible d'évaluer précisément ses performances ou ses capacités. La commercialisation de la machine et la durée de l'éventuel tarif réduit restent elles aussi à préciser.

articles.title: China’s DRAM Specialist CXMT Eyes NAND Flash Entry - EE Times
articles.text:
The NAND flash market is likely to have a new player, and it’s from China. ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT), which has already shaken up the DRAM market, is reportedly preparing to enter NAND flash to capitalize on a global memory shortage driven by surging demand from AI servers. Data centers need more solid-state drives (SSDs)—built around NAND flash—to store AI workloads.
According to Reuters, the company is setting up an R&D production line for NAND chips at its new fab in Beijing. Moreover, CXMT has established a research institute in Beijing, where projects include the development of NAND flash technology. Reuters also quoted an unnamed startup in China that is currently in talks with CXMT to use its NAND chips in storage products for AI systems and supercomputers.
First and foremost, it’s noteworthy because CXMT is moving beyond its core DRAM business. China’s twin memory stars, CXMT and Yangtze Memory Technologies Corp. (YMTC), have so far operated strategically in two major memory segments: CXMT is China’s largest DRAM manufacturer, and YMTC leads the NAND market in China.
However, in April this year, Reuters reported that YMTC had sent low-power DRAM samples to customers as it weighed entry into CXMT’s core market. YMTC expects customer feedback by the end of 2026, which will help it decide whether to start DRAM production. Now CXMT is considering a foray into the NAND flash market.
On the surface, it may seem that CXMT and YMTC are readying to move into each other’s memory turf. However, both CXMT and YMTC are backed by China’s national semiconductor fund and local governments. CXMT grew with backing from Hefei, the provincial capital of Anhui province in eastern China; YMTC expanded with backing from Wuhan, the provincial capital of central Hubei province.
A flash window of opportunity
A closer look at CXMT and YMTC encroaching on each other’s memory territories shows it’s about more than sparking direct competition in China’s domestic market. CXMT’s entry into NAND could inevitably generate friction over domestic equipment distribution, cleanroom tooling quotas, and specialized engineering talent from regional institutions. However, it also eliminates single-supplier vulnerabilities for memory consumers in China.
Memory industry leaders Samsung and SK Hynix have maintained commanding positions across both DRAM and NAND markets, and Micron has followed suit, though it initially lagged in NAND flash. The dual-memory portfolio allows chipmakers such as Samsung to absorb market downturns by continuously shifting capital between DRAM and NAND operations.
Both CXMT and YMTC likely want to become one-stop shops for DRAM and NAND, just like their bigger rivals Micron, Samsung, and SK Hynix. The timing couldn’t be better, amid a global memory shortage driven by AI server demand that industry executives expect to persist through at least 2027.
Both CXMT and YMTC could gain global market share by competing aggressively on price as memory supplies remain tight. However, according to the Korean newspaper Chosun Ilbo, that represents a longer-term competitive threat for global rivals rather than an immediate supply response.
At a time when the memory troika—Micron, Samsung, and SK Hynix—has prioritized capital spending on DRAM and high-bandwidth memory (HBM), limiting additions to NAND flash capacity and worsening shortages in this segment mark a window of opportunity for China’s largest memory chipmaker.
But the question is: How viable is this move? CXMT has neither announced a full commercial capacity target nor a publicly detailed production timetable.
Can CXMT pull it off?
Apparently, CXMT’s NAND plan is a work in progress. NAND flash is among the most capital-intensive undertakings in the semiconductor industry. It requires distinct tooling configurations and chemical supply chains, as well as completely different patent architectures compared to DRAM.
NAND manufacturing entails specialized process technology, production equipment, quality controls, and long-term design validation. Therefore, moving from an R&D line to commercially competitive volume production would involve substantial technical and financial challenges.
While the company is awash in cash after a blockbuster IPO, access to advanced chipmaking tools still poses significant challenges amid U.S. export controls. On the technical front, the shift from DRAM fabrication to vertical 3D NAND manufacturing creates steep operational challenges. DRAM relies on precise lateral photolithography to pattern dense capacitor networks at tiny dimensions, while 3D NAND devices are manufactured vertically.
So, CXMT, which spent the past decade developing a competitive DRAM technology, will most likely spend the next decade expanding beyond DRAM and into the NAND flash realm. This strategic expansion into flash memory also marks an inflection point in mainland China’s broader campaign to solidify semiconductor self-reliance across critical supply chains.

CXMT IPO: Where China’s Largest DRAM Maker Stands?
ChangXin Emerging as China’s First & Only DRAM Maker

articles.title: 9 Must-read lessons about friendship from classic books
articles.text:
9 Must-read lessons about friendship from classic books
Discover 9 powerful friendship lessons from classic books that teach loyalty, trust, forgiveness, courage, and the value of true companionship.
Friendship is one of literature's most enduring themes. Long before social media and instant messaging connected people across the globe, authors were writing about companionship, loyalty, trust, and the challenges that come with maintaining meaningful relationships.
Classic books continue to resonate because the lessons they offer about friendship remain relevant regardless of age or era.
Whether it's standing by someone during difficult times, learning to forgive mistakes, or finding strength in a loyal companion, these stories remind us what true friendship looks like.
9 Timeless lessons about friendship from classic books
1. True friends stand by you in difficult times: Charlotte's Web by E.B. White
The friendship between Wilbur the pig and Charlotte the spider is one of the most touching relationships in children's literature. When Wilbur learns that his life is in danger, Charlotte does everything she can to save him.
Their bond teaches an important lesson: real friendship isn't measured by convenience. True friends support one another when challenges arise, even when helping requires sacrifice. Charlotte's loyalty shows that friendship is often revealed through actions rather than words.
2. Differences can strengthen a friendship: The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes by Arthur Conan Doyle
Sherlock Holmes and Dr. Watson could hardly be more different. Holmes relies on logic and observation, while Watson brings empathy, practicality, and emotional intelligence.
Yet these differences are exactly what make their friendship work. Together, they balance each other's strengths and weaknesses. Their relationship reminds us that meaningful friendships don't require identical personalities; sometimes contrasting qualities create the strongest partnerships.
3. Friendship requires loyalty: The Lord of the Rings by J.R.R. Tolkien
Few friendships in literature are as inspiring as the bond between Frodo Baggins and Samwise Gamgee. Throughout their dangerous journey, Sam remains loyal despite exhaustion, fear, and uncertainty.
Their story demonstrates that loyalty is one of the foundations of lasting friendship. Being a good friend means showing up consistently, especially when circumstances become difficult. Friendship grows stronger when people remain dependable through adversity.
4. Friends help us become better people: Anne of Green Gables by L.M. Montgomery
Anne Shirley's friendship with Diana Barry becomes one of the most cherished relationships in classic literature. Together, they share adventures, dreams, mistakes, and personal growth.
Their friendship highlights how friends can encourage us to be more confident and courageous. Supportive relationships often help people discover talents and strengths they might never have recognised on their own.
5. Forgiveness is essential for lasting friendships: Little Women by Louisa May Alcott
The March sisters experience disagreements, jealousy, misunderstandings, and hurt feelings throughout the novel. Yet despite their conflicts, they repeatedly choose forgiveness and understanding.
No friendship is perfect. People make mistakes and occasionally disappoint one another. Little Women reminds readers that strong friendships survive because people learn to move beyond conflicts rather than allowing them to destroy the relationship.
6. Friendship can be a source of healing: The Secret Garden by Frances Hodgson Burnett
At the beginning of the novel, Mary Lennox is lonely, unhappy, and emotionally withdrawn. Through her growing friendships with Dickon and Colin, she gradually transforms into a happier and more compassionate person.
The story illustrates how genuine friendship can have a healing effect. Sometimes the support, encouragement, and companionship of others can help people overcome isolation and emotional struggles.
7. Friendship means accepting imperfections: Winnie-the-Pooh by A.A. Milne
Pooh and his friends have very different personalities. Eeyore is pessimistic, Tigger is energetic, Rabbit is organised, and Piglet is often anxious. Despite their differences, they continue to care for one another.
This classic story teaches that friendship isn't about finding perfect people. It's about accepting others for who they are, including their flaws, quirks, and unique characteristics.
8. Trust is earned through actions: The Wind in the Willows by Kenneth Grahame
Mole, Rat, Badger, and Toad share a friendship built on trust and mutual support. Even when Toad's reckless behaviour creates problems, his friends continue guiding him toward better choices.
Their relationship demonstrates that trust develops gradually through consistent actions. Friends earn confidence by being reliable, honest, and willing to help when needed.
9. Friendship is one of life's greatest treasures: The Great Gatsby by F. Scott Fitzgerald
Although The Great Gatsby is often remembered for its themes of ambition and the American Dream, the relationship between Gatsby and Nick Carraway offers another important lesson. Nick remains one of the few people willing to see Gatsby's humanity beneath the glamour and mystery.
The novel suggests that genuine friendship is rare and valuable. In a world often focused on status, success, and appearances, authentic human connections remain among life's greatest gifts.
Final thoughts
The best friendships aren't built overnight. They are strengthened through loyalty, understanding, patience, and shared experiences. Classic books remind us that friendship is not simply about having someone to spend time with; it's about finding people who support us, challenge us, and help us grow.
Whether it's Charlotte's sacrifice for Wilbur, Sam's loyalty to Frodo, or Anne's bond with Diana, these stories continue to offer lessons that remain just as meaningful today as when they were first written.

articles.title: CISA orders feds to patch Zyxel flaw exploited for data theft
articles.text:
Attackers are now actively exploiting a high-severity vulnerability in Zyxel GS1900 series switches, according to the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA).
The flaw (tracked as CVE-2026-7273) stems from a stack-based buffer overflow in the CGI program that lets threat actors without privileges on the local area network (LAN) execute OS commands via maliciously crafted HTTP requests.
Zyxel released security updates to address this issue on June 16 and advised customers to upgrade their firmware "for optimal protection."
While Zyxel has yet to update its advisory to confirm active exploitation of this flaw, CISA added CVE-2026-7273 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog on Monday and ordered Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies to secure their switches against ongoing attacks by Thursday as mandated by Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04.
"This type of vulnerability is a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and poses significant risks to the federal enterprise," the cybersecurity agency said.
"While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of KEV Catalog vulnerabilities."
| Affected model | Affected version | Patch availability | 
|---|---|---|

Although CISA has not released details on attacks abusing CVE-2026-7273, threat intelligence company GreyNoise said in a Monday report that it spotted the first signs of exploitation last Thursday.
According to GreyNoise, a suspected Chinese-speaking malicious cyber actor (MCA) has compromised nearly 1,000 Zyxel GS1900 switches as part of a campaign that targeted over a dozen other vulnerabilities affecting a wide range of software and tech products.
"GreyNoise discovered the MCA targeted ZyXEL GS1900 Smart Managed Switches globally with a novel exploit of CVE-2026-7273. As of 17 September 2026, this is the first publicly documented case of exploitation in the wild of this vulnerability," it said. "The MCA successfully exploited and exfiltrated sensitive data from 996 ZyXEL switches across 48 countries."
Zyxel devices are often targeted because many internet service providers worldwide provide them as default, out-of-the-box equipment for new internet service contracts.
In February, the company warned that it had no plans to patch a pair of actively exploited zero-day bugs (CVE-2024-40891 and CVE-2024-40891) affecting end-of-life routers still available for sale online. Instead, the company "strongly" advised customers to replace routers with newer products whose firmware was already patched.
CISA currently tracks 13 Zyxel vulnerabilities impacting the company's routers, switches, firewalls, and NAS devices that have been or are still exploited in the wild.
Zyxel claims that over 1 million businesses use its networking solutions across 150 markets worldwide.

articles.title: "Simplemente no encajaba": la estrella de 'Harry Potter' Emma Watson rechazó uno de los mayores éxitos de los Oscar
articles.text:
Hace ya casi siete años que no vemos a Emma Watson en una película de cine. No ha dejado la interpretación de forma oficial, pero se ha tomado un parón consciente para centrarse en su vida privada, su carrera académica, su activismo político y varios proyectos detrás de la cámara. Cuándo volverá a ponerse delante del objetivo es, a día de hoy, una incógnita.
Lo que sí sabemos es que hace 10 años, la actriz iba a protagonizar una película que no solo se convirtió en la sorpresa del año, sino que además acabó llevándose seis Oscar. Pero un blockbuster de mil millones se le cruzó en el camino.
Hermione y algo más. A Watson se la conoce, cómo no, por su Hermione Granger, pero su carrera va bastante más allá: la comedia 'Las ventajas de ser un marginado' (2012), el remake en acción real de Disney 'La Bella y la Bestia' (2017) o la adaptación literaria 'Mujercitas' (2019). Y estuvo a un paso de sumar a esa lista uno de los grandes éxitos de los Oscar de la última década: 'La La Land' (2016), de Damien Chazelle.
El papel era suyo. Antes de que Emma Stone se subiera al barco, el personaje de Mia Dolan, la joven actriz ambiciosa que se enamora del pianista de jazz Sebastian (Ryan Gosling), estaba pensado para Watson. Lo que la obligó a tirar la toalla fueron los preparativos, largos y exigentes, de 'La Bella y la Bestia'.
Ella lo cuenta así. En una entrevista con SiriusXM, recogida por Far Out Magazine, la protagonista de 'The Bling Ring' lo explicó sin rodeos: "'La Bella y la Bestia' no era una película en la que pudiera meterme sin más. Sabía que tenía clases de equitación, que tenía que bailar, que me esperaban tres meses de clases de canto y que para eso tenía que estar en Londres sí o sí. [...] No era una película en la que pudiera dejarme caer en paracaídas. Tenía claro que me la iba a tener que trabajar y que estaba atada a un sitio concreto. Así que, en cuanto a fechas, simplemente no encajaba".
Cambió un Oscar por mil millones. Mala decisión, desde luego, no fue: con una recaudación mundial de más de 1.200 millones de dólares, 'La Bella y la Bestia' se convirtió en la segunda película más taquillera de 2017, solo por detrás de 'Star Wars: Los últimos Jedi', que llevó a más gente a las salas.
Lo que pudo ser. El musical de Chazelle tampoco se quedó corto: 447 millones de dólares de taquilla frente a un presupuesto de apenas 30 millones, es decir, un exitazo inesperado en toda regla. Y, de propina, le dio a Emma Stone su primer Oscar.

articles.title: Kenya’s new payments bill could force banks to share customer data
articles.text:
Kenya’s central bank is proposing new rules that would let it require banks and payment providers to share customer data with licenced third parties, opening the door to open banking in one of Africa’s biggest digital-payments markets.
The draft National Payment System Bill, 2026, would require payment providers to build systems that can securely share customer data for “open finance purposes.” It would also give the Central Bank of Kenya (CBK) the power to require providers to enable that sharing once customers have given consent.
The proposal could loosen banks’ and mobile money providers’ control over customer relationships by allowing licenced fintechs to access customer data. That could turn data locked inside banks and M-PESA into a new battleground, giving fintechs a chance to compete for customers without having to own the accounts where their money sits.
“Each payment service provider or payment system operator shall use systems that are capable of securely sharing customer data with third parties for open finance purposes,” the draft bill read.
The bill does not name the third parties directly, but its licensing schedule creates two categories. Payment initiation service providers could execute payments on a customer’s behalf, while account information service providers could pull data and give customers a single view across accounts.
Neither category would need to hold customer funds to operate, unlike electronic money issuers and wallet providers. The bill requires the latter to keep customer money in trust accounts at a bank.
The bill is less specific on how access would work, saying CBK “may require” providers to enable data sharing after customer consent and “shall make regulations to give effect to this section.” Details on what data can be accessed, under what conditions, and at what cost would be left to subsequent CBK regulations.
Kenya’s proposal would cover banks and mobile money providers, opening their data to licensed payment initiation service providers and account information service providers, the two new fintech categories the bill creates, once the central bank issues regulations spelling out the access mechanics.
If Kenya’s parliament passes the law, players will have one year to comply with the new requirements.
“Upon the commencement of this Act, any person providing payment services shall, within one year of the commencement, comply with the provisions of this Act,” the proposed bill read.
The draft would also compel all financial and payment service providers to use systems compatible with competitors’ systems as part of a renewed interoperability push.

articles.title: Le HomePod avec écran se précise : Siri AI, reconnaissance faciale, modèles… voici ce qui vous attend
articles.text:
Nombreux sont ceux qui espéraient la présentation de l’écran d’accueil intelligent d’Apple, le nouveau HomePod, lors de la keynote de la rentrée de l’entreprise. En fin de compte, aucune mention de cet appareil, l’entreprise à la pomme a choisi de se concentrer sur l’iPhone 18 Pro, l’iPhone 18 Pro Max et l’iPhone Duo. Quid du nouveau HomePod alors ? Sa commercialisation a-t-elle été repoussée ? Il semble que non, selon le toujours très bien informé Mark Gurman. Le journaliste de Bloomberg est même venu apporter quelques informations sur ce nouvel appareil domotique.
Le centre névralgique de la maison
Mark Gurman décrit le HomePod comme « le centre névralgique de notre maison ». Ce hub domotique centralisera tous les appareils connectés, les appels vidéo, l’interphone et les contenus multimédias, tout en donnant un accès direct aux services et applications d’Apple. Il présente par ailleurs un écran au format presque carré, une connectivité étendue via le Wi-Fi domestique, une caméra frontale, des microphones et une interface qui combine les fonctionnalités d’iOS, de tvOS et de watchOS. Sans surprise, le HomePod se synchronise avec l’iPhone au moment de la configuration. Deux modèles seront proposés à la vente : une version sur pied, à placer sur un meuble du salon par exemple, et une version murale.
L’intelligence artificielle sera au cœur de l’expérience
Le HomePod a été en grande partie conçu autour de Siri AI. En réalité, l’appareil est prêt depuis maintenant des mois, mais le nouvel assistant d’Apple ne l’était pas. Ce dernier a maintenant été officiellement déployé auprès du grand public et Apple peut maintenant pleinement l’intégrer à ses nouveaux produits. Le HomePod serait d’ailleurs actuellement testé par certains employés d’Apple au sein de leur maison.
Nous l’avons déjà mentionné, le HomePod intègre une caméra frontale. Celle-ci proposera une fonction de reconnaissance faciale. Ainsi, l’appareil sera en mesure d’identifier les différents membres d’une famille et de personnaliser ses réponses et ses recommandations. À ce titre, Mark Gurman soulève un point particulièrement intéressant : Apple semble être parvenu à intégrer un système de reconnaissance faciale dans le fin écran du HomePod. Selon le journaliste de Bloomberg, cette petite prouesse technologique pourrait préfigurer l’arrivée de Face ID sur les prochaines générations d’iPhone Duo. Pour rappel, il s’agit de l’une des concessions qu’a dû effectuer Apple sur son premier iPhone pliant.
Enfin, notons que le HomePod intégrera un nouveau système d’exploitation basé sur Siri AI, et que l’écran disposera de sa propre interface d’accueil, de widgets et de cadrans d’horloge similaires à ceux de l’Apple Watch.
Il reste la question de la date de commercialisation. Le mois dernier, Mark Gurman rapportait qu’Apple effectue un réaménagement de certains espaces de ses magasins afin de pouvoir exposer le HomePod, mais aussi l’Apple TV 4K de nouvelle génération. Toujours selon Gurman, la commercialisation de ces deux produits devrait avoir lieu dès le mois d’octobre prochain. Il ne reste donc plus beaucoup de temps à attendre. Rappelons tout de même que Siri AI est toujours bloqué en Europe…

articles.title: iPhone 18 Pro teardown highlights mechanical camera aperture and a major thermal redesign
articles.text:
Bottom line: The teardown specialists over at iFixit recently got their hands on Apple's new iPhone 18 Pro series. On paper, not a whole lot has changed compared to last year's model but once the team started diving into the nuts and bolts, they found several noteworthy changes that could help influence your purchasing decision.
The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are the first smartphones from Apple to ship with a variable aperture. Samsung experimented with a similar mechanism years ago with some of its Galaxy and Note devices, but that run was short lived. Apple's implementation features six tiny aperture blades that physically open and close to precisely control how much light reaches the camera sensor.
Each blade is roughly the thickness of a human hair, and utilizes strategically spaced slots and holes to aid in their movement. When activated, they slide past one another with extreme precision that leaves virtually no room for error. It's an impressive feat of engineering, although some will argue that the juice isn't worth the squeeze in this instance.
Indeed, if one of the aperture blades were to get stuck or otherwise fail, you'll almost certainly need to replace the entire camera assembly to fix the issue.
Fortunately, swapping out the camera module is "painless," iFixit said.
Another commonly serviced component – the battery – is also relatively easy to replace, although getting to it can be a bit tricky. While the back glass panel of the new iPhone can be opened with ease, there are no serviceable parts when taking this avenue aside from the wireless charging coil. That means you have to go in from the front to get to the battery and contend with the glued-down screen.
In three of the four iPhones iFixit operated on, the plastic frame around the display broke during removal.
Elsewhere, the new iPhones feature custom packaging that places the A20 Pro silicon die side by side with the memory – effectively removing the memory from the chip's thermal path. This allows the SoC to attach directly to the vapor chamber cooling system for improved thermal performance. According to Apple, the redesigned vapor chamber enables up to a 40% gain in sustained performance over the previous generation.
All things considered, Apple's iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max earned a provisional score of 7/10 for repairability. For most users, the best course of action will simply be to protect the device with Apple Care and leave any major repairs to the experts.
Image credit: iFixit

articles.title: Google leva multa de 403 milhões de euros por coletar dados de localização • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Google leva multa de 403 milhões de euros por coletar dados de localização
Órgão de proteção de dados da Irlanda concluiu que configurações violaram as regras europeias de privacidade entre 2018 e 2020.
A Comissão de Proteção de Dados da Irlanda (DPC, na sigla em inglês) multou o Google em 403 milhões de euros (cerca de R$ 2,3 bilhões) nesta segunda-feira (21/09). A penalidade é fruto de uma investigação sobre a forma como a gigante de tecnologia coletou, tratou e reteve dados de localização de usuários.
A autoridade irlandesa concluiu que a big tech violou as regras do Regulamento Geral sobre a Proteção de Dados (GDPR), segundo a agência Reuters. As infrações foram identificadas em três recursos oferecidos aos usuários entre 2018 e 2020:
Essa não é a primeira vez neste ano que o Google sofre uma sanção milionária na Europa. Em julho, a Comissão Europeia puniu a big tech em 890 milhões de euros (R$ 5,2 bilhões) por favorecimento dos seus serviços na busca e na Play Store no Android, incluindo ferramentas proprietárias de compra e formas de pagamento.
Em janeiro, outra derrota: a Justiça do bloco europeu decidiu pelo pagamento de uma multa que chega a R$ 25 bilhões por abuso de posição dominante, em um caso que se arrastava desde 2016.
A apuração apontou falhas graves na transparência, na legalidade e na equidade do tratamento desses dados pessoais.
Segundo o comissário-adjunto do DPC, Graham Doyle, os usuários muitas vezes não tinham conhecimento do uso das próprias informações geográficas para fins de monetização ou perfilamento comportamental, e que isso leveva a perda do “controle sobre seus dados pessoais”. Ainda segundo Doyle, a “retenção de dados de localização dos usuários por mais tempo do que o necessário agravou essa perda de controle”.
Além do pagamento da multa, o regulador emitiu uma ordem para que a companhia adapte todas as suas práticas de processamento de localização às normas da legislação europeia em um prazo máximo de seis meses.
O DPC abriu o processo formalmente em 2020, impulsionado por denúncias formais apresentadas por diversas entidades de defesa do consumidor na Europa.
Por sediar sua matriz europeia em Dublin, o Google responde diretamente ao órgão irlandês, que atua como autoridade líder na União Europeia para a maioria das grandes corporações de tecnologia dos EUA sob as regras do GDPR em vigor desde 2018.
A sanção de 403 milhões de euros representa a quarta maior multa já aplicada pelo regulador irlandês contra empresas de tecnologia — em um montante histórico que já ultrapassa a marca de 4 bilhões de euros (R$ 23 bilhões) em penalidades acumuladas no país. Mas o cerco continua: segundo a Reuters, o Google ainda é alvo de outras três investigações formais em andamento na Irlanda.

articles.title: BDC is Canada’s sole entrant in investor network for NATO defence accelerator | BetaKit
articles.text:
The Business Development Bank of Canada (BDC) is continuing its defence push by joining a NATO accelerator international investor network.
The news: NATO announced an initial list of groups joining an investor network associated with its NATO Defence Innovation Accelerator for the North Atlantic (DIANA) on Monday. It includes BDC as Canada’s only entrant, alongside European investors like Expeditions and US defence primes like Lockheed Martin.
BDC and other selected groups will connect with companies that have gone through the NATO DIANA accelerator, in the hopes of boosting defence investment.
From the source: “Being part of this network gives us a direct line into where our 32 NATO allies are investing, innovating, and creating demand,” Peter Dawe, BDC’s vice-president of defence strategy and a recently retired Major General, said in a video posted to BDC’s LinkedIn page.
The context: The NATO DIANA accelerator connects companies with military end-users, mentors, and capital to help develop and validate new technology. With the NATO DIANA Capital Network, it will be putting them in front of a swathe of new investors, too. Several Canadian companies have been accepted to the accelerator, including Québec rocket company Reaction Dynamics and Ottawa defence software startup Tactiql (also a 2026 BetaKit Most Ambitious honouree).
This also follows BDC taking a much bigger role in the defence industry. The Crown corporation has launched a $6-billion CAD defence platform across its banking and investment divisions.
Final thought: This isn’t the only opportunity for Canada to take a bigger role in defence investments. In July, the country entered negotiations to join a subdivision of the NATO Innovation Fund. It is also creating an international defence bank to back defence contracts for allied governments and companies—an initiative that BDC CEO Isabelle Hudon has been deeply involved in. However, it’s still unclear which Canadian city will host the bank.

articles.title: Gehaltsreport 2027: In diesen IT-Jobs ist die Bezahlung am besten
articles.text:
Gehaltsreport 2027: In diesen IT-Jobs ist die Bezahlung am besten
Spezifisches Branchenwissen gepaart mit Digitalkompetenz: Dieses Profil ist laut dem Gehaltsreport der Personalberatungsagentur Michael Page, der t3n exklusiv vorliegt, im nächsten Jahr auf dem deutschen Arbeitsmarkt besonders gefragt – und zwar in allen Branchen.
Die Analyse der internationalen Vermittlungsgesellschaft beruht dabei unter anderem auf Interviews mit Kandidaten und Unternehmen sowie auf der Auswertung der firmeneigenen Datenbank. Außerdem wurden branchenspezifische Studien und Trendberichte sowie Gehaltsvergleiche für gefragte Jobprofile berücksichtigt.
In der IT bleibt die Nachfrage im nächsten Jahr laut der Personalberatungsagentur zwar stabil – allerdings ächzt die Branche unter dem herrschenden Transformations- und Effizienzdruck. Besonders Senior- und Architekten-Profile sind laut der Analyse gefragt. KI verändert weiterhin Aufgabenprofile, besonders Fachkräfte mit Architektur-, Integrations- und Steuerungskompetenzen können hier profitieren.
Rolle des Cybersecurity-Experten am meisten gefragt
Im nächsten Jahr sind laut der Markstudie Cloud-, Daten- und Cybersecurity-Experten besonders gefragt. Das spiegelt sich auch in den Prognosen für die Gehaltsbänder wider: Von allen analysierten IT-Berufen liegt das Gehalt des Information Security Officer am weitesten vorn. Im Durchschnitt verdient man hier 105.000 Euro im Jahr, teilweise ist sogar ein Gehalt bis 130.000 Euro möglich.
Auch Data Engineers können mit einem Durchschnittsgehalt von 90.000 Euro im Jahr rechnen, über 110.000 Euro kommen sie aber laut den Prognosen der Personalberatungsagentur nicht. Ebenfalls weit vorn sind die Service-Manager, die an der Schnittstelle zwischen Kunden, Fachbereichen, IT-Betrieb und externen Dienstleistern arbeiten und mit einem Durchschnittsgehalt von 87.500 Euro rechnen können – mit Luft nach oben. Projektmanager befinden sich ebenfalls in den Top 4 der bestbezahlten IT-Jobs 2027. Sie können ebenfalls mit einem Durchschnittsgehalt von 85.000 Euro punkten.
1st-Level-Support, Service-Techniker und Roll-out-Techniker am schlechtesten bezahlt
Mitarbeitende am Helpdesk oder am Service-Desk, Service-Techniker sowie Roll-out-Techniker, die neue IT-Lösungen einführen werden in der Branche am schlechtesten bezahlt. Ihr Gehalt bewegt sich zwischen 36.000 bis 50.000 Euro. Technisch spezialisierte Administratoren, die im Second-Level-Support arbeiten, bewegen sich ebenfalls auf der unteren Skala bei den Gehältern in der IT. Sie verdienen im Durchschnitt 51.000 Euro, Löhne bis zu 60.000 Euro sind allerdings auch möglich.
Administrationsrollen im unteren mittleren Bereich
Mitarbeitende im Third-Level-Support, die sich mit besonders komplexen Themen befassen und etwa Bugs analysieren und beheben, verdienen laut der Analyse zwischen 59.000 und 69.000 Euro. System- und Netzwerkadministratoren bewegen sich zwischen 58.000 und 75.000 Euro.
Software- und Data-Rollen gefragt
Im Software- und Data-Bereich haben Data Engineers die meisten Chancen auf das höchste Gehalt, hier sind Löhne bis zu 110.000 Euro möglich. Auch Projektmanager haben hier hohe Verdienstchancen, im Durchschnitt verdienen sie 85.000 Euro. Data Scientists kommen dagegen laut dem Gehaltsreport höchstens auf 90.000 Euro.

articles.title: Amazon bloquea a Muse, la IA de Meta que puede comprar en línea por ti
articles.text:
Amazon le ha cerrado la puerta a Muse, el asistente de IA de Meta que puede controlar tu ordenador. A unos días de que se convirtiera en una de las aplicaciones más populares en móviles y debutara en la Mac, Muse no podrá realizar compras en Amazon usando tu cuenta de usuario. El gigante del comercio electrónico aseguró que el agente de Meta compraba en su tienda sin permiso ni aviso previo, por lo que decidió bloquearlo.
De acuerdo con GeekWire, Amazon bloqueó a Muse durante la noche del domingo. Cualquier usuario que intente usar al agente de Meta para comprar en la plataforma se encontrará con una notificación informando que no es posible. “El acceso continuo por parte de un agente de IA no autorizado viola las Condiciones de Uso de Amazon”, señala el mensaje.
Según Amazon, Meta nunca solicitó permiso para que su asistente operase dentro de la plataforma. La tecnológica añadió que Muse no se identifica cuando navega por el sitio y, según análisis internos, llega a capturar y almacenar las credenciales de los usuarios. Este punto es el que más ha preocupado a Amazon y sería el pretexto ideal para bloquear a la IA en su tienda en línea.
La IA de Meta no es la única que ha bloqueado Amazon
Aunque el bloqueo de Muse ha tomado relevancia por la relación que existe entre ambas empresas (Meta usa los chips Graviton para su IA), lo cierto es que no es el primer agente que sufre este veto. Amazon lleva varios meses cerrando la puerta a agentes externos de Google y OpenAI, así como a Perplexity, con quien tiene abierto un proceso judicial debido al navegador Comet.
Un portavoz de la compañía dijo que las aplicaciones que compran en tu nombre deben operar de forma transparente y respetar las decisiones de cada plataforma. Meta aseguró hace unos días que su agente no tiene visibilidad sobre las contraseñas ni métodos de pago de los usuarios, ya que usa un segundo sistema llamado Sentinel para procesar todas las operaciones.
Amazon añadió que su objetivo es proteger la experiencia de compra, pero también hay otra razón de peso: los anuncios. La plataforma tiene un negocio publicitario que registra ingresos de 68.000 millones de dólares al año. Esta cifra depende de que los usuarios naveguen por las páginas de su tienda y vean productos patrocinados, algo que no ocurre cuando le pides a un agente de IA que se encargue de comprar por ti.
Sumado a esto, Amazon tiene herramientas de compra asistida, como Alexa for Shopping y Buy for Me, que sí se identifican como una IA ante los comercios.
Muse no podrá acceder a una de las tiendas más grandes de internet
Meta aseguró hace unos días que su agente no tiene visibilidad sobre las contraseñas ni métodos de pago de los usuarios, ya que usa un segundo sistema para procesar todas las operaciones. A diferencia de Meta AI, Muse funciona como un agente capaz de ejecutar tareas completas en tu móvil o Mac. La IA se conecta con tu cliente de correo, calendario, notas y opera dentro de una máquina virtual segura con un navegador propio.
Para evitar que las cosas se salgan de control, los de Mark Zuckerberg implementaron un agente adicional conocido como Sentinel. Este aprueba cualquier acción que Muse envíe a internet y se encarga de procesar el sistema de pago y otros datos de forma segura, de modo que los servicios de Meta no puedan acceder a ellos. Muse se conecta con otros servicios y aplicaciones a través de APIs públicas, pero cuando el sistema no tiene una de estas, navega por la web como si fuera una persona.
Aunque esto es una mala noticia para los usuarios de Muse, la realidad es que no todos pueden comprar en línea usando la IA de Meta. Esta función solo está disponible en Estados Unidos a través de plataformas de terceros como Stripe o 1Password. De momento no existe una fecha definida para ofrecerla en otros países, como España, México, Argentina o el resto de América Latina.

articles.title: With Tabby, a former accountant is using AI to make accountants obsolete | TechCrunch
articles.text:
In May of 2025, Ahad Ali was a successful accountant, overseeing a team of 20 people and handling more than 2,000 returns a year. “We did bookkeeping, accounting, sales tax, taxes, everything,” Ali says. It was a stable business, and one that would have been easy to stay in.
But Ali started to notice something. His work was increasingly dictated by the frictions of accounting software, which was rarely designed with actual accountants in mind. He became frustrated with specific accounting software like QuickBooks, and soon he became frustrated with the entire idea of SaaS-based accounting.
“I realized that small businesses don’t need better accounting software,” Ali told TechCrunch. “They need less accounting software. They need something that just does it for them.”
Now, Ali is building just that. His product, Tabby, is designed to be a real-time bookkeeping interface, handling clients’ paperwork as it gives them up-to-the-minute data on their business’s profit and loss. Using Plaid to import live account data, Tabby uses AI to quickly build a real-time dashboard for a business’s financial health.
There’s also a version of Tabby for accounting firms that want a smarter alternative to QuickBooks, but Ali’s goal is to go direct to the end user as often as possible. As Ali sees it, products like Tabby have a chance to automate away the work of bookkeeping once and for all, turning it into a monthly charge on the order of internet access or payroll services. If successful, it could seriously change the calculus of operating a small business.
“You can say QuickBooks digitized bookkeeping,” Ali told TechCrunch, “but we want to make [that visible software layer] nonexistent.”
So far, it seems to be working. Fourteen months in, Tabby has 5,500 small businesses using the platform, with roughly $100,000 in annual recurring revenue. The team is still just seven people — Ali, his technical co-founder, four engineers and a go-to-market specialist — and in the process of raising $1 million in pre-seed funding. When I spoke to Ali, his team was just preparing to launch Tabby Talk, a natural language interface for the product.
There’s plenty of competition in the accounting space, particularly now that AI has shaken things up. Ali has his eyes focused on QuickBooks, which is still the biggest player — but he’ll also be facing well-funded startups like the Sequoia-backed Rillet, as well as the major labs’ own finance tools. It’s a daunting task, but Ali thinks that Tabby can carve out a niche by focusing on the same small- to medium-sized firms that helped his accounting business thrive.
“Everything we see is making us believe that there’s a path for other players, because the space is big,” Ali told TechCrunch. “There’s 30 million more businesses.”
Learn more about Tabby and the other innovative startups involved in our prestigious Startup Battlefield 200 competition at TechCrunch Disrupt, happening October 13-15 in downtown San Francisco.

articles.title: D&D Miniatures Buying Guide: How to Choose Scale, Material, and Format for Your Table - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Almost every miniature listing leads with a millimetre number, and almost none of them explain it. That number is not total height.
It is a rough measurement taken from the base up to the character’s eye line for an average human-sized figure, which is why a figure labeled 28mm usually stands around 30 to 35mm from base to crown. Once you know that, the labels stop being mysterious and start being a compatibility hint.
The measurement that actually decides whether a figure works on your battle map is the base. A standard D&D battle grid uses one-inch squares, or about 25.4mm, and a typical humanoid miniature sits on a round base roughly 25mm across. That is why both 28mm and 32mm figures drop into a single grid square without overhang. If you have ever wondered why two different scale labels both seem to work at the same table, this is why.
Scale and base size are separate decisions, and confusing them is the most common mistake. The scale number mostly affects how a figure reads next to its neighbors: proportions, paint surface, visual weight. The base diameter is what determines grid occupancy. A medium creature with a 25mm base occupies one square. Many large creatures step up to a base in the 40 to 50mm range and straddle the space around them. Huge and gargantuan monsters can span two or more squares, and if you are running a fight with a dragon, that footprint matters more than the height printed on the box.
D&D’s own size categories, Small through Gargantuan, map loosely onto this. Medium covers most player characters and sits at the standard humanoid base. Large covers ogres, big cats, and plenty of mid-tier threats. The mapping is a hobby convention rather than a hard specification, and it varies between manufacturers, so treat it as a strong tendency instead of a rule you can measure against.
For most players, the practical difference between 28mm and 32mm is small. Both read as a normal-sized hero on a one-inch grid, and both coexist on the same table without looking broken. The difference shows up in consistency with an existing collection, in how much surface area a painter has to work with, and in visual presence when a figure stands beside a larger ally or enemy. If you are building on a collection you already own, matching what you have usually beats chasing a new standard. If you are starting fresh, pick one and stay with it.
Scale is also a convention, not an exact science. Two figures from different makers can carry the same nominal number and still look noticeably different in build and proportion. When that happens, the mismatch usually reads as a posture or base difference rather than a scale error, and a base swap or a slight repositioning closes most of the gap.
When you are standing in a storefront filter or scanning a product page, run the checks in this order: confirm your grid, confirm the base diameter, and only then think about the nominal scale. That sequence answers the only question that matters at the table: will this figure physically do what I need it to do?
Painted or unpainted: what you are actually signing up for
The painted-versus-unpainted label looks like a quality signal. It is really a time commitment, and it is worth reading that way. Pre-painted figures arrive table-ready out of the pack. Unpainted plastic and resin figures typically need assembly, cleanup, a primer coat, and paint before they look finished on the table. Neither state is better than the other; they serve different players.
Unpainted is not a defect. It is a hobby step, and it is the reason a lot of people get into miniatures in the first place. What the label does not tell you is how much work the step involves. A single character figure with moderate detail might be an evening’s project. A bulk box built around a themed encounter can carry dozens of figures and turn that evening into a season. When a listing advertises unpainted miniatures in quantity, the figure count is a stronger signal of the work ahead than any description of the sculpt.
The multiplication effect is the part buyers underestimate. Forty figures at one clip and one figure at one clip are not the same hobby, even though both carry the same “unpainted” tag. Preparation work scales with detail level too. A figure with crisp recesses, layered cloth, and fine armor takes longer than a smooth silhouette, not because the technique is harder but because there is more surface to address.
Do not assume a specific product is paint-ready, primed, or table-ready out of the box unless the listing or the manufacturer’s own material says so plainly. Modern manufacturing has blurred the line between materials, and a product that looks like primed grey plastic in a photo may not behave that way in hand.
This is also where your purchase format decision starts to intersect with your calendar. Bulk packs lower the per-figure cost, but they only deliver that value if you actually intend to prepare the figures. If you want to open a box and play tonight, budget for pre-painted, or accept that this is a painting project as much as a gaming one. A useful self-check before you buy: how many hours this season are you willing to spend on preparation versus play? Answer that honestly, and the painted decision usually makes itself.
Plastic or resin: durability, painting, and price tendencies
Material is the attribute storefront filters handle least helpfully. Most pages reduce it to a single word, which hides the fact that plastic, resin, and the various plastics used for pre-painted and board-game figures behave very differently in hand.
Start with handling. Plastic tends to be more flexible, so thin parts such as spears, sword blades, and delicate limbs can bend rather than snap. That flexibility is a real advantage for figures that get picked up, moved, packed into a case, and unpacked again every session. Resin tends to be more rigid. Normal assembly and tabletop use hold up well, but a drop is less forgiving, particularly on protruding detail. Community collectors describe the pattern clearly from experience: the materials that hold detail well are often the more brittle ones.
Painting behavior splits the same way. Many painters prefer resin because fine detail reads more easily, washes settle into recesses more predictably, and highlights separate cleanly on complex texture. Plastic can absolutely reach a high standard, but it usually takes more effort to achieve the same definition, especially on softer or smoother surfaces. This is not a knock on plastic. It is a statement about where the effort goes.
Price positioning tends to follow production reality. Plastic is usually cheaper in a large set and widely available across product lines, since injection molding makes big runs economically sensible. Resin figures are often pricier per model, reflecting finer detail, smaller batches, and made-to-order production. Those are tendencies, not universal rules.
The rule of thumb for most D&D tables is simple: choose plastic for figures you will handle and transport constantly, and consider resin when detail and painting are the reason you are buying at all. Keep in mind that the word “plastic” covers real variability. A figure made for repeated handling behaves differently from one made for painting and display, and the two are not interchangeable just because the box says plastic.
Singles, sets, or bulk packs: a value and prep-time trade-off
Once scale, painted state, and material are settled, the purchase format question reads as a price question. It is better understood as a precision-versus-effort question.
- Singles buy precision. You want a specific monster for a specific encounter, or a specific character to represent someone at the table, and you buy exactly that. The cost per figure is the highest of the three formats, and building a collection one figure at a time is slow.
- Encounter sets and themed bundles cover a scenario in a single purchase. They trade the precision of singles for convenience and a lower cost per figure, and they cut the time you would otherwise spend hunting down individual pieces across multiple listings.
- Bulk packs push the cost per figure down furthest and give you volume to draw from. The trade-offs are duplicates, uneven quality across the box, and a meaningful increase in painting and storage work. A bulk pack that saves money per figure still costs you evenings.
If you are comparing bulk options, the truly useful number on the listing is the per-count unit price, not the headline total. A 60-figure box and a 20-figure box can look very different in price until you divide by figure count.
Treat retail prices as checkable, not fixed. Listings change, sales end, and pre-order status flips. Look at the current product page rather than committing a number to memory, and be skeptical of any guide that quotes stable prices.
A workable sequence: decide what this season’s campaign actually needs, then choose singles where the campaign is specific and a bulk base layer where it is broad. Most players end up somewhere in between, with a few precise purchases and one honest bulk box to cover the chaff.
Matching miniatures to a campaign, encounter, or party
Buying by category is easier than buying by campaign, but campaign-shaped buying is what makes a collection useful. Here is how that plays out for a few common table situations, then a sequence that works whatever your campaign looks like.
A goblin-heavy arc changes what your core needs to be. If most of your early sessions are goblinoids and their hangers-on, a matching block of low-tier raiders is worth more than a spread of single-use monsters, because a single fight can drain ten identical figures at once and you want them to read as a group on the grid. A single signature leader figure for the arc anchors the bigger scenes, and after that you can stop.
An undead arc pulls the same way, with a different target. Skeletons and zombies fill the same “recurring low-tier block” role, and the signature figure is usually the caster or commander behind them rather than a beast. The point is not a specific product; it is that the creature types your campaign actually repeats shape what you buy well before the storefront filters do.
A conversation-led campaign buys differently again. If your table spends most sessions talking, scheming, and traveling, your highest-use figures are party characters, key NPCs, and the occasional large set-piece creature for the scene the arc has been building toward. Ten identical monsters cover very little of that table’s real demand.
With those scenarios in mind, the sequence is the same each time.
Step 1: List what recurs
Before buying anything, write down the creature types and party roles that actually appear repeatedly in the campaign you are running or playing. Two or three lines is enough. Which of the three scenes above describes your table most often will already tell you a lot about what belongs on that list.
Step 2: Prioritize a common enemy core
Common low-level enemies are the highest-use purchase in almost any campaign. Ten matching figures of the same type cover a single fight cleanly and read as a group on the grid, which is often better than ten mismatched individual monsters that each appear once.
Step 3: Add one or two signature large creatures
A campaign is usually anchored by a handful of scenes with a major threat. Picking one or two large creatures that fit the campaign’s theme gives you more table presence than a dozen mid-tier generic monsters.
Step 4: Reserve character figures for the party
Player character miniatures are the most consistently used figures in any collection. They show marching order, they show positions during exploration, and they are the ones players actually care about seeing. This is the place where spending more per figure is easiest to justify.
Step 5: Reassess after a few sessions
A collection that grows in response to what the campaign actually did is far more useful than one that grew in anticipation of what it might do. Large collections do not guarantee that the right figure is findable mid-session, and a small, well-chosen set often plays better than a large, unsorted one.
When not to buy a miniature: standees, board-game minis, 3D printing, and digital tokens
Physical miniatures are one answer to “what represents this monster on the grid,” not the only answer. The substitutes below come from community and retailer comparisons, so treat the individual claims as general tendencies rather than measured findings.
Flat standees and cardboard pawns are generally cheaper per figure, lighter, and easier to store and carry, which makes them useful for players who travel to sessions. The trade-offs are typically lower-resolution art on budget lines, front-facing art with a plain or blurred back on many products, and a single fixed pose. If you search for high-resolution standees specifically, most of those downsides shrink considerably.
Board-game minis can deliver a lot of figures for the money, but scale and quality vary across boxes, and each set needs checking against your grid and your existing collection before you commit. A board game is a good source if you also want the game. It is a weaker source if you only want the figures.
3D printing offers design freedom you cannot get from a stocked catalog, at the cost of equipment, time, and finishing work. Since the figures come out of the process unpainted and often need support cleanup, printing and miniature-buying share the same preparation-heavy trade-off discussed earlier; you simply move the source of the figure upstream. Browser-based generation is one low-equipment entry point into that path. With Meshy, you can start from a text description or a set of reference images and receive a textured 3D asset, with GLB, FBX, and STL among the export formats the platform supports. Using several consistent reference views can give the sides and back that a single image never shows more information to work with, which tends to improve the silhouette and proportions of the result. From there you rotate the model, check it from angles the prompt did not cover, adjust the text or images and regenerate, retopologize or retexture it when the shape is close but the topology or surface is not, and export. Once the file is out, whether it works for a mini is a question for your slicer and printer settings, not something the generation step settles on its own.
Digital tokens remove physical storage entirely, which is a real advantage for DMs with limited space or frequent remote sessions. The cost is a different table experience. Physical distance becomes abstract, and the tactile quality of moving a figure does not carry over. That is a preference question, not a quality question.
Laid out side by side, the trade-offs sort by cost, portability, durability, immersion, and preparation effort rather than by any single winner. Standees and tokens win on cost and storage. Printed and purchased miniatures win on presence. Board-game minis sit in the middle on price and coverage. There is no universal answer, only the answer that matches the session you are actually running.
Reading storefront filters: what product lines and set names tell you
Once your scale, painted state, material, and format decisions are made, the filter panels on a storefront stop being noise. Product line families and their rough release windows exist as orientation so you can decode the labels you are about to click. Treat that as background, not as a set list or a release table to copy. Those details shift, and a guide’s snapshot ages faster than the storefront does.
The practical outcome is that you can now navigate the same filters a catalog presents with a decision already in mind. Availability and pre-order status still change, so confirm on the current product page rather than relying on any single overview, including this one. Do not assume one store’s category structure applies everywhere. Use the labels to understand what a filter means, then read the specific listing for what you are actually buying. When the shelf is one click away and you already know your grid, your material, your format, and your campaign’s recurring needs, the browsing stops being guesswork.
FAQ
What scale are D&D miniatures, and does 28mm or 32mm matter on a one-inch grid?
Both scales sit comfortably on a one-inch (25.4mm) grid square. The scale number is roughly a base-to-eye measurement for an average human-sized figure, not total height. The base diameter is what determines grid occupancy, so for most players the 28mm versus 32mm choice comes down to consistency with an existing collection rather than rules compatibility.
What does “unpainted” actually require before a figure is ready for the table?
Typically assembly, cleanup, priming, and painting before play. Pre-painted figures arrive table-ready. The work scales with figure detail and quantity, so a bulk box carries substantially more preparation time than a single character figure. Do not assume a specific product is primed or paint-ready unless the listing says so.
Is plastic or resin better for miniatures I will handle and transport often?
Plastic tends to be more flexible and forgiving on thin parts, which suits repeated handling and travel. Resin tends to be more rigid, holds finer detail well, and is often preferred by painters, but it is less forgiving when dropped. These are general tendencies that vary by manufacturer and intended use.
How do I decide between buying singles, an encounter set, or a bulk pack?
Match the format to the need. Singles buy precision for a specific encounter or character. Encounter sets cover a themed scenario efficiently. Bulk packs lower the cost per figure at the price of duplicates and more preparation work. Compare bulk options using per-count unit pricing rather than headline totals, and check current listings rather than trusting quoted prices.
Which miniatures should I buy first for a new campaign or a new party?
Start with the creature types and party roles that recur most. A small core of common low-level enemies covers the highest number of fights. Add one or two signature large creatures for the campaign’s key scenes, and reserve character figures for the player characters themselves. Then reassess after a few sessions and fill gaps the campaign actually exposed.
When is a standee, board-game mini, or digital token a better choice than buying a miniature?
When cost, storage, or portability matter more than table presence for a given session. Standees and cardboard pawns are generally cheaper and easier to store. Board-game minis provide volume but vary in scale and quality. Digital tokens remove physical storage entirely but change the table experience. The right answer depends on which trade-off your table cares about least.

articles.title: 3 fintech companies join GIZ-backed venture debt programme in Egypt - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Egyptian fintech companies AMAN Holding, Bokra and Erada Finance have joined Scale It Forward, an initiative launched by GIZ Egypt and enpact to advance the adoption of Venture Debt in Egypt.
The Scale It Forward programme brings together financial institutions and high-growth scaleups with the aim of expanding access to non-dilutive financing, building the financial sector’s capacity to design and deliver venture debt products, and creating a structured pathway for the adoption of Venture Debt within Egypt’s entrepreneurial ecosystem.
The three financial institutions signed framework agreements with enpact during a launch ceremony in Cairo, becoming the programme’s first financial institution partners and marking their commitment to exploring and piloting venture debt solutions designed to support high-growth businesses seeking alternative financing options.
Under the programme, GIZ Egypt will provide participating financial institutions with technical assistance to support the design and deployment of venture debt products within a controlled pilot environment. AMAN Holding, Bokra and Erada Finance will also gain access to a pipeline of selected scaleups.
As part of the pilot, they will also identify promising scaleups from the programme pipeline, while selected businesses will receive tailored support to prepare for Venture Debt financing. Financial institutions will provide venture debt financing starting from the equivalent of EUR5,000 (US$5,800) per business, matched by EUR5,000 in non-repayable financial support provided through the programme.
“Today’s signing event represents the official launch of the Scale It Forward programme. By bringing together three forward-looking financial institutions, AMAN, Erada Finance, and Bokra, we are taking a significant step towards establishing venture debt as a practical and scalable financing solution that enables ambitious scaleups in the Egyptian market to scale their businesses, create jobs, and grow without sacrificing equity,” said Rawan Bassam, country manager of enpact in Egypt.

articles.title: Les GeForce RTX 60 retardées à 2028 ? Une nouvelle source confirme la rumeur
articles.text:
Alors que la plupart des GeForce RTX série 50 voient leur prix augmenter, NVIDIA ne semble pas devoir sortir les RTX série 60 avant 2028.
Tout semble indiquer que NVIDIA ne proposera pas de nouvelle avancée majeure en matière de GPU grand public avant 2028 : les nouvelles cartes graphiques GeForce RTX série 60 feraient ainsi l'impasse sur 2027.
2027 : année blanche pour NVIDIA ?
Le calendrier des prochaines GeForce de NVIDIA semble prendre du retard. Selon une nouvelle information relayée par VideoCardz, la famille de GPU identifiée sous le nom de code GR20x ne ferait finalement pas son apparition avant 2028. Ces puces sont considérées comme la base de la future génération GeForce RTX série 60, qui devrait exploiter l’architecture Rubin.
L’information provient notamment de Kopite7kimi, un leaker régulièrement à l’origine de précisions sur les produits NVIDIA. Celui-ci avait précédemment évoqué une commercialisation au cours du second semestre 2027. Il indique désormais que le projet GR20x est prévu pour 2028, précisant que le calendrier aurait donc été une nouvelle fois repoussé. Le leaker affirme par ailleurs vouloir limiter ses prochaines publications tant que des informations plus précises ne seront pas disponibles.
À ce stade, NVIDIA n’a toutefois annoncé ni les futures GeForce RTX série 60, ni leur dénomination commerciale officielle, ni une quelconque date de sortie. Il convient donc de prendre ce nouveau calendrier avec une certaine prudence. De la même manière, alors que l'on trouve déjà de pseudo-caractéristiques techniques pour la génération Rubin, il est important de préciser que NVIDIA n'a encore rien publié de concret à ce propos.
Plusieurs indices convergent vers 2028
Cette nouvelle estimation n'est pas complètement isolée. En effet, il y a seulement quelques jours, nous avions déjà relayé les propos d'un autre informateur bien connu du monde NVIDIA, Kepler_L2.
Nous avions alors mis en parallèle les « révélations » de deux personnes : d'un côté, Kepler_L2 donc et, de l'autre, Moore's Law is Dead, amateur de vidéos sensationnalistes et loin de toujours être fiable. Ce dernier avait indiqué que, justement, tout était prêt du côté de NVIDIA et que la sortie des premiers modèles de GeForce RTX série 60 arriverait non seulement en 2027, mais même au cours du second trimestre de l'année. Dans moins d'un an donc.
Une affirmation sobrement critiquée par Kepler_L2 qui, en réponse, indiquait simplement « il a tort ». Kepler_L2 évoquait plutôt le fait que seul AMD allait lancer sa nouvelle génération de GPU en 2027 et encore, la firme dirigée par Lisa Su ne le ferait qu'au travers d'une seule puce, l'AT2. Le reste de la gamme RDNA 5 serait lancé, comme les GeForce RTX série 60, en 2028. Clairement, la précision apportée par Kopite7kimi renforce cette position.
La convergence de ces deux informations – qui, toutefois, ne citent pas directement leurs sources – renforce l’hypothèse d'un changement de calendrier chez NVIDIA.
Pour les joueurs, un tel calendrier signifierait une présence particulièrement longue de la génération RTX 50 sur le marché. La situation est d’autant plus notable que le rafraîchissement RTX 50 SUPER a lui-même connu plusieurs changements de calendrier rapportés par différentes sources et que… ces cartes ne sont toujours pas commercialisées. NVIDIA pourrait ainsi conserver plus longtemps sa génération actuelle avant de lancer une véritable nouvelle architecture grand public.

articles.title: Building intelligent enterprises: why developers must bridge code and business reality
articles.text:
Building intelligent enterprises: why developers must bridge code and business reality
At DevSparks Hyderabad, Subish Ram traced a decade-long shift from RPA to agentic AI and made the case that in addition to building technology, the ability to understand business will define developers going forward.
For years, software engineering in large enterprises followed a well-defined boundary: business teams outlined requirements, and centralized IT units built the software. Today, the rapid rise of generative AI (Gen AI), low-code tools and agentic workflows is upending that model.
Speaking at DevSparks Hyderabad, Subish Ram, Digital Products and Services leader, EY GDS highlighted that the enterprise delivery engine is undergoing a fundamental structural reset. Drawing from a decade of automation across the global EY organization, which supports a 400,000+ strong workforce across its member firms, Ram emphasized that engineering teams can no longer operate in technical silos.
“The standalone IT team that just does software development is no longer that prominent,” Ram observed. “More of that is shifting into the business side of the house. We need people who understand the business, who can talk the language of the business and bring technology into that.”
The shift from central IT to business prototyping
The enterprise automation journey began nearly a decade ago with robotic process automation (RPA) tackling repetitive back-office tasks. Over time, rule-based RPA evolved into intelligent workflows and it has now advanced into full-fledged agentic AI systems that orchestrate end-to-end business functions like finance, procurement and HR.
With tools like Replit, Cursor and enterprise-approved copilots widely accessible, nontechnical teams are taking development into their own hands. Tax consultants, HR leaders and finance analysts are increasingly building the first cut of internal tools themselves.
“The first cut of development today is happening at the business end,” Ram noted. “What comes to the technology team is: Can you help us scale this? Can you deploy this? Can you do security testing?” This transition changes the developer's core mandate. In the near future, business units will handle basic prototyping, testing, and AI-assisted bug resolution. The engineering community, in turn, will be responsible for system architecture, integration, governance and enterprise-grade scalability.
Solving the enterprise ROI and cost equation
While experimentation is surging, Ram offered a candid perspective on enterprise AI adoption: calculating clear return on investment (ROI) remains a major hurdle.
Unlike traditional RPA, where replacing manual hours generated clear, immediate cost savings, AI deployments entail substantial recurring token consumption, infrastructure, and maintenance costs.
“ROI is aspirational right now,” Ram explained. “If you automate a complete reporting process using AI, and it costs hundreds of thousands of dollars each year just to keep running, there is often no immediate ROI. We have seen business cases where token costs rivaled human costs.”
Ram stressed that end customers ultimately care about productivity, efficiency and the bottom line, rather than whether a solution uses Python, traditional dashboards or autonomous agents. To create sustainable value, developers must focus on building reusable accelerators, improving token economics and reducing AI consumption costs.
Domain context is the new technical moat
To remain indispensable in an AI-native world, engineers do not need to become domain consultants, but they must understand the mechanics of the domain.
“You don’t need to become a chartered accountant to build a solution for finance, but you need to understand the language they use and what business outcome they expect,” Ram concluded. As AI tools democratize code generation, a key competitive advantage for developers will be understanding the business problems they are solving.

articles.title: BigCommerce alerts merchants of data breach linked to Ribon apps
articles.text:
Ecommerce platform BigCommerce has alerted multiple merchants to data breaches after attackers compromised credentials for third-party Ribon applications and used them to inject malicious scripts into online stores.
The cloud-based Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) ecommerce platform confirmed the credential compromise on September 17 and immediately removed the apps to protect its customers.
UK-based online spirits vendor Master of Malt is one of the BigCommerce customers that received the notification. The retailer said the attacker accessed shopper information.
The hacker used the compromised credentials to access shopper data in BigCommerce environments between September 13 and September 17, the company said.
In updates on the incident, Master of Malt says impacted shopper details include full names, email addresses, phone numbers, and shipping postal addresses.
“It looks like hackers were able to compromise a BigCommerce Application key held by Ribon, which they were able to use to gain access to customer data held on their system,” Master of Malt stated.
BigCommerce supports over 1,200 third-party applications and integrations, including Ribon, an application operated by Be A Part Of, a brand operated by Fastr, specialized in shopping experience optimization.
The e-commerce platform says it stores account passwords and payment card information separately and that this type of data was not exposed.
In a statement for BleepingComputer, BigCommerce said that the attacker compromised credentials for Ribon and Ribon 1.5 applications.
"On September 17, 2026, Commerce confirmed that credentials belonging to third-party applications Ribon and Ribon 1.5, owned and operated by 'Be A Part Of,' a Fastr company, had been compromised and used to inject malicious scripts into a small number of merchant storefronts."
The company underlined that its systems or the BigCommerce platform were not breached.
"Acting in the best interest of our customers and their shoppers, we uninstalled the application from affected stores to revoke the attacker's access, notified those merchants directly, and are providing log data to support the developer's investigation," the company told BleepingComputer.
Master of Malt reported the incident to the UK Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO) and noted that it may extend well beyond its own customers, potentially to hundreds of other stores.
Law firm Emery Reddy is seeking potential claimants linked to the incident, saying several retailers are currently notifying customers about data exposure linked to the Ribon app key theft, without naming any.
BleepingComputer has contacted Be A Part Of and Fastr for more information about the incident but we have not received a response by publication time.
The incident is similar to a 2024 breach affecting electronics accessory maker ZAGG, where attackers compromised the third-party FreshClick BigCommerce app and injected payment-skimming code into its online store.
At the time, BigCommerce told BleepingComputer that its platform was not breached and removed the compromised app from customers’ stores.
However, unlike the ZAGG incident, where attackers captured payment information entered by customers during checkout, the Ribon attackers used a compromised application key to access existing customer records through BigCommerce.
