Source : CBS News

articles.title: Pour la première fois, on a capté des signaux radio sur une exoplanète
articles.text:
Ne ménageons pas le suspense pour les fans d’extraterrestres : non, aucune civilisation alien ultra-développée n’est impliquée dans cette découverte. Une équipe d’astronomes étatsuniens a découvert un signal radio émis par l’exoplanète Beta Pictoris b, et ils détaillent leurs données dans une étude parue sur le serveur arXiv et repérée par le site Science News.
Avant de rentrer dans le vif du sujet, il faut savoir que jamais un tel signal n’avait pu être capté sur une planète en dehors de notre Système solaire. Ces ondes ont bien pu être étudiées lorsqu’elles venaient d’étoiles ou de galaxies lointaines, mais jamais d’une planète. En revanche, l’étude n’a pas encore passé le stade de relecture par les pairs, et reste donc, pour l’instant, à prendre avec des pincettes.
Émission radio à 63 années-lumière
Les travaux reposent sur des données acquises par le radiotélescope MeerKAT, en Afrique du Sud. Ce grand champ composé de plusieurs dizaines d’antennes paraboliques en plein désert a pour but de repérer des signaux issus de structures diverses à travers la galaxie.
C’est ainsi que les auteurs ont mis la main sur un signal en particulier dont ils ont pu remonter à la source. Cette source, c’est Beta Pictoris b, une exoplanète géante dont la masse est environ dix fois supérieure à celle de Jupiter et qui orbite autour de son étoile à environ 63 années-lumière de la Terre. Découverte en 2008, elle se situe à 8 ou 9 unités astronomiques de son étoile (une unité astronomique correspond à la distance entre la Terre et le Soleil), et elle a pu être imagée directement à plusieurs reprises, son orbite quasiment vue par la tranche étant particulièrement scrutée par la communauté scientifique.
Ici, les auteurs ne sont pas certains à 100 % que le signal vienne bien d’elle, mais ont pu déterminer qu’il venait très probablement d’une planète, et que l’étoile elle-même n’était pas impliquée. D’autres analyses devraient venir confirmer ou infirmer cette hypothèse, mais si c’est bien le cas, cela soulève une autre question : comment cette planète émet-elle des signaux ?
Des aurores gigantesques
En effet, si les réactions thermonucléaires d’une étoile peuvent suffire à expliquer ces phénomènes, une planète seule devra trouver d’autres stratagèmes. Et ici, il semblerait que ces signaux soient émis par des aurores.
Si le mécanisme est bien connu sur la Terre, il a aussi pu être vu sur Mars, ainsi que sur Jupiter et Saturne. Dans la plupart des cas, les aurores se déclenchent quand des particules chargées, venues de l’étoile ou de l’environnement immédiat de la planète, percutent la haute atmosphère et son champ magnétique. Le phénomène est d’autant plus fort que le champ magnétique est puissant.
Et justement, pour ce qui est de Beta Pictoris b, nous sommes devant un champion de sa catégorie, puisque son champ magnétique dépasse les 1 000 gauss (l’unité qui mesure les champs magnétiques), contre seulement 0,5 gauss pour la Terre. Dans ces conditions, il n’est pas étonnant que les aurores créées lors de l’interaction avec l’étoile soient particulièrement impressionnantes. Jusqu’à pouvoir être « vues » depuis la Terre ?

articles.title: Cet aspirateur balai laveur Roborock s'incline à 180°C pour passer sous tous les meubles et sous la barre des 150 €
articles.text:
Le Roborock F25 RT est un aspirateur balai laveur positionné comme l’option la plus accessible de cette gamme, qui l’est encore plus avec les 210 € de réduction sur Cdiscount.
Le Roborock F25 RT est un des aspirateurs-balais laveurs les moins chers du marché, surtout quand il s’affiche avec pas moins de 58 % de réduction sur Cdiscount. Alors ce n’est pas le dernier modèle de la marque, qui propose un modèle de 2e génération sur son site, mais il permet quand même de bien aspirer et de laver en un seul passage, avec auto-nettoyage à l'eau chaude et tête inclinable à 180°. C’est clairement un aspirateur pour les petits budgets si vous cherchez un appareil pour l’entretien régulier des sols durs.
Voici le Roborock F25 RT à 149 € au lieu de 359 € sur Cdiscount
Pourquoi choisir le Roborock F25 RT ?
- Parce qu’il fonctionne bien sur sols durs si vous cherchez un appareil pour passer un coup régulièrement.
- Le rouleau qui se nettoie (presque) tout seul avec la station qui lance un cycle d'autonettoyage à l'eau chaude 90°C suivi d’un séchage à l’air chaud.
- Il passe sous les meubles et rase les plinthes avec son inclinaison à 180°, qui lui permet de passer sous les meubles de 12-13 cm et à moins d'un millimètre des bords.
Un balai laveur pensé pour l’entretien régulier
Il faut voir le Roborock F25 RT comme un appareil à utiliser pour perpétuer un entretien quotidien. Il n’est pas vraiment pensé pour les gros ménages ponctuels, malgré son efficacité en aspiration, ce n'est pas un nettoyeur vapeur haute pression. Il a une autonomie annoncée de 35 minutes en mode Eco, des réservoirs de 870 ml d’eau propre et 720 ml d'eau sale pour un poids de 3,57 kg. Sa puissance d’aspiration de 20 000 Pa et le rouleau à 450 tours/minute lui permettent d’entretenir un logement de taille moyenne. Et ça remplace le duo historique balai + serpillière.
Un F25 plus abordable que les autres modèles de la gamme
Le Roborock F25 RT, on l’a dit, est le plus abordable de la gamme, où on peut retrouver le F25 classique, le F25 Ace et le F25 Ultra. Le modèle RT conserve la puissance d'aspiration et l'autonettoyage à 90°C, mais fait l’impasse sur l’écran, les roues motorisées et les modes avancés. Même l'autonomie est plus limitée, donc face à des concurrents comme le Tineco Floor One i5 Stretch ou le Dreame H12 Pro FlexReach, il se défend sur le prix et la simplicité, mais reste en retrait sur les fonctions plus poussées.
✅ Les points forts
- La puissance d’aspiration de 20 000 Pa
- Le rouleau à 450 tours/minute pour un nettoyage quotidien
- Le système d'autonettoyage à l'eau chaude à 90°C avec séchage à air chaud
- L'’inclinaison à 180° avec nettoyage des bords près des plinthes
- Le poids contenu pour une bonne maniabilité
❌ Les limites
- L’absence d’écran LED fait qu’il n’y a pas d’indication claire sur le niveau de batterie, du mode choisi ou autre
- L'’autonomie limitée à 35 minutes en mode Éco
- Pas d’application ni de capteurs avancés
- Les performances en baisse sur les taches anciennes et incrustées
Pour quelques jours le Roborock F25 RT est à -58 % sur Cdiscount
Le Roborock F25 RT est intéressant pour qui cherche un premier balai laveur autonome, efficace au quotidien, sans payer pour des fonctions superflues. Il convient bien aux petits budgets et aux surfaces réduites, comme un studio type T2/T3 ou les petites pièces de vie.
En revanche, si vous avez de grandes surfaces ou que vous visez un nettoyage profond de taches incrustées, il vaut mieux passer aux F25 supérieurs, ou carrément chez la concurrence mieux équipée. Pour le F25 RT, il faut accepter un usage régulier et raisonnable.

articles.title: CISA alerts of active exploitation of three Linux kernel flaws
articles.text:
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) is warning that hackers are exploiting three Linux kernel vulnerabilities, one of them rated critical.
The three security issues were added separately last week and have severity ratings ranging from medium to critical. One of them, tracked as CVE-2025-39964, existed in the Linux kernel for 14 years.
CISA marked all three flaws with the highest priority for federal agencies, ordering them to apply available security updates and mitigations by the end of today.
The three vulnerabilities are:
- CVE-2025-39964: a race condition in the kernel’s AF_ALG cryptographic socket interface that allows concurrent writes to corrupt per-socket state and potentially crash systems or alter cryptographic results.
- CVE-2026-53266: an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the Linux kernel’s ebtables SNAT implementation that can cause an ARP address rewrite to modify shared file-backed memory without first making the affected packet range writable.
- CVE-2025-39682: a Linux kernel TLS receive-path logic flaw that mishandles zero-length records queued for later processing, potentially allowing different TLS record types to be processed together when kTLS is in use.
CISA says [1, 2] the vulnerabilities have been exploited in attacks but has not revealed any details about the incidents or the nature of the threat actors.
Offensive security company STAR Labs found CVE-2025-39964, saying that its researchers found the issue with no help from an AI system. They demonstrated the vulnerability by achieving privilege escalation and container escape in Google’s kernelCTF.
For CVE-2025-39682, there are public exploits available, as also confirmed by Red Hat in its security bulletin. Red Hat also confirmed a known exploit available for CVE-2026-53266.
Researcher Kimmo Suominen has published a technical analysis and patch-status tracker for CVE-2026-53266 on GitHub, outlining a potential privilege-escalation path involving modifications to file-backed memory.
However, the researcher notes that the proposed exploitation chain is inferred by analogy with Dirty Pipe and has not been demonstrated with public exploit code.
CISA has marked all three flaws as requiring “forensic triage.” This means that for every affected asset, federal agencies need to examine it for signs that exploitation already occurred.
Currently, none of the three flaws is flagged as exploited by ransomware groups.

articles.text:
L’Arabie saoudite aussi s’intéresse aux voitures électriques. Pour le moment, elle passait principalement via son fonds d’investissement (le PIF), notamment pour investir dans Lucid, mais elle vient de franchir un cap en présentant, via un communiqué de presse, les deux voitures électriques de sa première marque nationale : Ceer Automotive.
La marque, fondée en 2022 sous la forme d’une coentreprise entre le PIF et Foxconn (le fabricant taïwanais des iPhone, entre autres), vient donc de présenter ses Ceer Exobot. Non, vous n’avez pas sous les yeux des concept-cars des années 1980, mais bel et bien des modèles qui seront vendus au public.
Un style hors du commun
Avec leur ligne en coin, leurs proportions folles et leurs portes papillon (baptisées Shahin Wing Doors et longues de trois mètres !), les Exobot Sedan et Exobot SUV auraient tout à fait pu être présentés par un Bertone en grande forme.
Nous sommes pourtant en 2026, et les signatures lumineuses à LED ainsi que les jantes de 23 pouces à l’avant et 24 à l’arrière sont de bons indicateurs. Les dimensions sont folles : la berline s’étale sur 5,26 m de long pour 2,10 m de large et 1,42 m de haut ; le SUV s’arrête à 5,01 m de long pour 2,10 m de large et 1,69 m de haut.
Que dire de plus ? Ceer semble être particulièrement fier de son pare-brise, à la fois le plus long (2,4 mètres) et le plus incliné (15°) de la production automobile. À l’intérieur, un écran incurvé de 48 pouces dit « pillar-to-pillar » court sur toute la largeur de la planche de bord. Il est accompagné d’une dalle de 10,4 pouces au centre pour les réglages et d’une troisième de 8 pouces pour les passagers arrière.
Comptez 402 litres de coffre pour le SUV et 424 litres pour la berline, des chiffres, il faut le dire, limités vu le gabarit des deux véhicules.
Une fiche technique qui n’a rien de révolutionnaire
Pour déplacer de beaux bébés, la base technique est identique sur les deux voitures. Les Ceer sont motorisées par une architecture trimoteurs (un à l’avant, deux à l’arrière) pour une puissance totale de 625 kW (850 ch) et 1 000 Nm, de quoi passer de 0 à 100 km/h en 2,6 secondes (2,9 s pour le SUV).
Côté batterie, un pack NMC (nickel – manganèse – cobalt) de 112 kWh est implanté dans le plancher, de quoi offrir 670 km d’autonomie pour la berline et 560 km pour le SUV… selon l’obsolète cycle NEDC, réputé pour être très optimiste et remplacé depuis de nombreuses années par le cycle WLTP en Europe, un peu plus cohérent.
    Pour aller plus loin
            WLTP, EPA, CLTC, NEDC : comment mesure-t-on l’autonomie des voitures (électriques) ?
            
Bref, des autonomies qui n’ont rien de révolutionnaire, et la recharge suit. Même si Ceer promet une architecture 800 volts, passer de 10 à 80 % de la batterie demandera « moins de 30 minutes », un score à vrai dire assez décevant quand la concurrence demande 10 à 15 minutes de moins.
Côté dynamique de conduite, Ceer annonce une direction électronique (steer-by-wire) associée à des roues arrière directrices pour gagner en agilité.
Les tarifs ne sont pas encore annoncés, tandis que les premières livraisons sont prévues pour début 2027. Les Ceer Sedan et SUV seront produites dans une usine flambant neuve à King Abdullah Economic City, où Lucid y construit également une usine.
La marque se concentre pour le moment sur le marché saoudien, mais espère pouvoir s’étendre à l’international, et prévoit déjà de lancer cinq autres modèles d’ici 2028. On leur souhaite bon courage.

articles.title: Uber Redesigns M3DB Sharding with Subclusters to Limit Failure Impact
articles.text:
Uber has redesigned shard placement in M3DB by introducing fixed-size subclusters to limit the impact of node failures, maintenance, and cluster scaling. The change addresses a limitation in the previous placement model, where a node failure could affect up to (n-1)/n of the cluster as shard dependencies grew.
M3DB is Uber's distributed time series database, where data is divided into shards and replicated across multiple nodes. Its placement algorithm determines shard ownership while enforcing isolation between replicas, such as keeping replicas in different racks or availability zones. Uber engineers emphasized that the original sharded placement model worked well for small-to-medium clusters but became more difficult to operate as clusters grew.
With the original model, any node could own a shard as long as replicas were not placed in the same isolation group. In a permissive configuration, this can create a dependency graph in which a topology change affects O(N) nodes. Even when isolation groups correspond to three zones for a replication factor of three, a node can share data with as much as 66.67% of the cluster. Uber says this can increase recovery activity and force maintenance operations to be serialized.
The new model partitions nodes into fixed-size subclusters, with each subcluster owning a distinct, nonoverlapping portion of the shard space. In Uber's example, a 12-node cluster with a replication factor of three and six nodes per subcluster contains two subclusters, each owning half of the shards. Within a subcluster, M3DB continues to distribute replicas across isolation groups.
Uber's comparison of conventional sharded placement and subclustered placement (Source: Uber Blog Post)
Scaling requires moving shards from existing subclusters to a new one. Uber uses a greedy algorithm that evaluates the effect of removing each candidate shard from the donor subcluster and selects shards that leave the remaining nodes as evenly loaded as possible. This avoids a separate rebalancing pass and the additional network transfer and bootstrap work that would result from moving shards twice. The algorithm uses O(S log S) sorting and O(S × N) simulation work, where S represents candidate shards, and N represents nodes in the subcluster.
M3DB's existing placement documentation similarly describes shard movement as a process in which destination nodes stream data from existing peers before taking ownership, making unnecessary shard movement an operational cost. Its placement model also uses isolation groups to prevent replicas from sharing a rack or availability zone.
The subcluster approach has constraints. It requires equal instance weights, scaling in multiples of the subcluster size, and a subcluster size that is a multiple of the replication factor. It also does not support changing the replica factor through AddReplica. During scaling, cross-subcluster shard sharing can occur temporarily, while only one partial subcluster is permitted at a time.
Shard distribution with greedy algorithm (Source: Uber Blog Post)
Uber retained M3DB's existing instance-level placement operations rather than introducing atomic subcluster operations. Uber team emphasized that this preserves compatibility with existing tooling and avoids triggering a large bootstrap operation in which many shards migrate simultaneously. M3DB's placement implementation now includes fields for subclustered placement and the number of instances per subcluster.

articles.title: Luz no fim do túnel: CEO da Acer prevê queda nos preços de PCs em 2027 • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Luz no fim do túnel: CEO da Acer prevê queda nos preços de PCs em 2027
Jason Chen prevê mais aumento nos preços de computadores até o fim de 2026. Mas a tendência deve se inverter no segundo semestre de 2027.
Representantes de companhias de tecnologia passaram os últimos meses fazendo previsões desalentadoras sobre a crise das memórias RAM. Mas Jason Chen, CEO da Acer, tem uma visão mais otimista sobre esse cenário: o executivo prevê que os preços dos PCs devem apresentar um pico em 2027, mas começar a cair no mesmo ano.
É claro que, para isso, o mercado terá que passar por alguns ajustes. Nesse sentido, Chen prevê que os preços de PCs ainda devem experimentar um aumento generalizado entre 5% e 20% até o fim de 2026.
Isso porque, presumivelmente, os preços de componentes ficaram defasados em relação aos valores repassados aos consumidores e, portanto, é necessário haver um reequilíbrio.
Porém, já no primeiro semestre de 2027, os preços deverão iniciar uma estabilização. Então, no segundo semestre do mesmo ano, os preços finalmente começarão a cair, ainda que não se saiba em qual proporção. Pelo menos é o que Chen dá a entender.
Mas fica a pergunta: como isso será possível se a demanda por memória RAM e outros componentes para computadores continua elevada?
A essa altura, você já sabe o que está por trás do aumento expressivo nos custos de memória RAM, chips de armazenamento e outros componentes: a expansão acelerada de data centers voltados a aplicações de inteligência artificial.
Mas, no entendimento de Chen, a indústria de PCs está recebendo suprimentos em escala suficiente para dar conta da produção. Não que não haja escassez. Mas, para o executivo, esse problema só é expressivo em determinados nichos atualmente.
O CEO da Acer também argumentou que os fabricantes de memória querem maximizar seus lucros pelo maior tempo possível, por isso, divulgam mensagens afirmando que os preços dos componentes “não vão cair até o ano 20 e alguma coisa”.
Chen acredita ainda que há mais um fator favorável a uma queda de preços: a crescente participação de fabricantes chineses no mercado de componentes para PCs. A própria Acer já estaria recorrendo a chips da chinesa CXMT em algumas de suas linhas de produtos.
É claro que a visão de um único executivo não representa o entendimento de toda a indústria. Além disso, temos que considerar que as declarações de Jason Chen foram dadas ao jornal taiwanês Money UDN, portanto, podem refletir o mercado asiático, e não o panorama global.
Mas, no meio de tantas previsões catastróficas, não há como não prestar atenção quando alguém do setor vislumbra um futuro mais otimista e, o melhor, relativamente próximo.

articles.title: Leuven-based Spott raises €18.3 million to build the AI-native operating system for recruitment agencies | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Spott, a Leuven-based AI-native applicant tracking system (ATS) and customer relationship management (CRM) platform for recruitment agencies, has raised €18.3 million ($21 million) in a Series A round.
The round was led by Balderton Capital with participation from Base10 Partners, Y Combinator and Fortino. The Series A funding follows a €2.8 million ($3.2 million) Seed funding round raised in March 2025.
“Lander, Manu and Samuel understood this overlooked problem because they had seen its operational and commercial impact first-hand. They have combined that insight with the technical ambition to rebuild recruitment’s core infrastructure and the speed at which customers are adopting Spott shows they have built the solution this market has been waiting for,” said Phil Chambers, Partner at Balderton Capital.
Founded in 2024 by Lander Degreve, Manu Vanderveeren and Samuel Smeys, Spott grew out of the trio’s experience advising recruitment businesses at McKinsey, Bain and BCG. During this time, they observed an industry open to modernisation but held back by outdated, disconnected software.
The company argues that human judgement accounts for only about a fifth of a recruiter’s workload, with the rest consumed by administrative tasks and candidate sourcing, which it says AI can handle, leaving people in charge of final decisions.
Spott serves recruitment firms across Europe, the US and APAC from its Leuven headquarters. Its core platform launched only six months after its Seed round, and the company says its revenue has grown more than tenfold since the start of 2026. It now counts hundreds of agencies as customers, including H.W. Anderson and the 200-person CGP Group, which has deployed the platform across 12 countries.
Recruitment agencies rely on a combination of legacy tools such as separate systems for candidate databases, sourcing, outreach, note-taking, and scheduling. Spott wants to defragment the space with an AI-native workspace capable of turning emails, CVs, and pipeline data, including candidate databases, into searchable and actionable intelligence. It says roughly 20% of the revenue currently comes from the APAC region and 15% from the US.
“During our work with recruitment businesses, we saw firms under intense pressure to cut costs and make more placements, while their recruiters lost hours moving information between outdated systems. Recruitment succeeds through trust and human judgement. Spott gives agencies control of their data and puts AI to work around their recruiters, freeing them to deepen relationships with candidates and clients,” said Degreve, co-founder and CEO of Spott.
The new funding will be used to support the company’s expansion into the US and APAC, new enterprise features, and hire additional engineers to build out agentic AI capabilities. Spott plans to open offices in Sydney and New York and grow headcount from 44 to around 60 by the end of the year.

articles.title: Peloton is back with a ‘cheaper’ folding treadmill
articles.text:
Last year, Peloton did a sweeping refresh of its hardware that added cameras, fans, and AI-powered software called Peloton IQ. This year, it’s zeroing in on its treadmill lineup — refreshing its two existing Treads and adding the new, more affordable Tread Flex into the fold.
Peloton is back with a ‘cheaper’ folding treadmill
Plus two other refreshed treadmills and a host of AI running features.
Peloton is back with a ‘cheaper’ folding treadmill
Plus two other refreshed treadmills and a host of AI running features.
At a New York City launch event, Peloton chief product officer Nick Caldwell told the press the $2,195 Flex — which can be folded upright to save 50 percent more floor space — was meant to address user feedback for a more easily stowed machine. When folded, the Flex purportedly has a smaller overall footprint than the Bike Plus. It also has caster wheels so it can be maneuvered more easily. For safety, the wheels can be locked in place, it has the existing Tread Lock passcode, and it has a slow-opening mechanism using a two-cylinder release. In person, it took about 25 seconds for the deck to lower fully. You don’t have to do anything or push the deck, and there’s no ka-thunk — it just sort of gently falls. That said, Peloton confirmed at the event that there are no sensor-based safety features.
While running, the Flex has a relatively quiet motor at 70 decibels. It’s hard to gauge exactly how quiet it is in a demo space, but it was notably quieter than other treadmills I’ve run on. I don’t think most people will have an issue running on the Flex’s shorter deck, but it might be a concern if you have particularly long legs. Like Peloton’s other treadmills, it has a swivel screen so you can do other types of workouts, but no camera, precluding it from some of the new Peloton IQ features (more on that below).
Meanwhile, its existing two treadmills have been rebranded as the $3,495 Tread Vision and $6,695 Tread Plus Vision. (The former is a $200 price increase, while the latter is the same price.) Here, the upgrades are more refinements. The Vision has a new deck that’s got better cushioning, redesigned jump buttons that let you go up and down for speed / incline, plus a redesigned tray for holding tablets, phones, and water bottles. The Tread Plus Vision also has the new jump buttons, plus a new “sled” mode that may appeal to Hyrox or Crossfit athletes. Both still have a swivel screen and motion tracking cameras that enable some new treadmill-related Peloton IQ features.
As far as software goes, all the treadmills are getting personalized pace. After about 10 running workouts, you’ll get a recommended pace targets that automatically populate within a workout. They may adjust over time as fitness improves. Peloton is also launching a new feature called ReRun, which lets you upload outdoor run course data recorded in the Peloton app or from a smartwatch into the treadmill so you can “re-run” them. That includes automatic incline adjustments based on outdoor elevation on a route. Peloton is partnering with NYRR so that users can “re-run” segments of the New York City Marathon course. At the event, press were told that the company is exploring partnerships for other famous races as well.
For the camera-enabled treadmills, Peloton is adding a running analysis feature. There’s a one-time calibration and then afterward, the movement-tracking camera will run in the background of subsequent workouts. Based on steps, cadence, vertical oscillation, and stride length, users will get a running efficiency score and tips on how to improve their form.
So far, Peloton’s big bet on refreshed hardware and AI hasn’t translated into earnings. At least, not with its existing user base. That may be why at the event, it seemed Peloton was keen to emphasize who it was hoping to reach with each treadmill. The Flex, for example, was repeatedly referred to as the ideal treadmill for walkers, hikers, and folks living in cramped New York City apartments. Its “cheaper” $2,195 price is also more in line with its bikes, though that’s relative considering you can buy other walking pads and treadmills for much less. On the other end of the spectrum, the Tread Plus Vision was described as the treadmill of choice for performance athletes. The Tread Vision was envisioned for multi-member households who might have people at varying fitness levels. (Various Peloton reps and instructors also pointed out the new redesigned tray as a great option for people who want an alternative to a walking pad — though it’s not possible to hook your laptop up to the display as a second monitor.)
Peloton has repeatedly identified the treadmill space as one it views as ripe for growth in earnings calls. Altogether, it’s clear that Peloton is hoping these new treadmills — but particularly the Flex — might attract new membership signups.

articles.title: Don’t be fooled by this summer of AI hype
articles.text:
Don’t be fooled by this summer of AI hype
Breathless claims about AGI and new capabilities fall apart pretty quickly under scrutiny.
It’s been a busy few months for AI hype. At the end of April, Anthropic claimed that its model Claude Mythos is better at finding software vulnerabilities than most security experts. Then we had the OpenAI–Hugging Face hacking incident, after which Anthropic (proudly) and Meta (reluctantly) disclosed similar incidents involving their models.
This was followed by Anthropic’s claim that one of its models had made a mathematical breakthrough; soon OpenAI claimed a mathematical breakthrough of its own. Most recently, Anthropic engineer Jacob Coxon went viral announcing his departure from the company, claiming that it and OpenAI are “racing straight towards self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives.”
Each of these events was mostly covered breathlessly by the press, often repeating the companies’ anthropomorphizing framings—which are designed to portray their software is not only powerful but incipient “artificial general intelligence.” So what is really going on? Are we witnessing a massive, civilization-changing set of technological breakthroughs, or is this marketing?
In all these incidents, massive fanfare from the companies (presented as mea culpas in illicit hacking cases) is accompanied by intense press coverage. Once there is time for experts in the relevant fields to examine what happened, a very different story emerges, but one that gets less media attention.
Regarding the “hacking” incidents, cybersecurity experts say the story is more about OpenAI’s negligence and failure to adopt basic, established security practices than about “models gone rogue” or “AI agents creating civilizations.”
As for the mathematical results, mathematicians who were initially “stunned” by OpenAI’s press release saying that its latest chatbot, Astra, solved problems that “have been open and seen no progress on the main result for at least a decade”—but they later realized that the results weren’t as “novel as first appeared.” Since then, mathematicians have accused the company of research misconduct and plagiarism, and they’ve reiterated that Astra didn’t make a “profound intellectual leap.” Just weeks later, OpenAI claimed its own mathematical breakthrough. Two days before, Tristan Buckmaster, a math professor at New York University’s Courant Institute, published a bombshell statement suggesting that OpenAI had stolen other people’s work and improperly attributed it.
Claims of incipient, dangerous superintelligence are not based in good scientific or engineering practice. Rather, they are narratives based in ideologies of transhumanism, eugenics, and wishful thinking about imagined future digital humans.
It’s worth thinking about why there is so much attention on computer programming and math as fields in which to apply large language models and related technology. Not only are they often elevated as the pinnacle of human intellectual achievement, but they involve problems where answers, once suggested, can be verified. The former property helps AI hype mongers sell the idea that they are building everything machines. The latter makes math and coding problems easier to tune systems for, since system output (sequences of likely words or pieces of computer code) can be evaluated without having to pay data workers to look at and annotate each one.
Mathematicians in particular have warned against corporations using their field in this way. A statement signed by hundreds of them says there is “currently a strong commercial incentive on the part of the technology industry to overstate the capabilities of their products” and asks policymakers to “consult with experts, including mathematicians, in forming policy decisions rather than relying on press releases or popular reporting of mathematical results.”
We echo this call and note that the illusion of speed and urgency promulgated by the tech companies is also a ploy to misdirect both policymakers and the public. Unfortunately, it sometimes works, such as with Senator Bernie Sanders’s well-meaning but ultimately misguided proposed legislation to prevent the development of “artificial superintelligence.”
Describing them as “superintelligence” or “rogue models” ascribes agency to products rather than to the companies building them. This framing markets these companies’ products as “superhuman” and, at the same time, helps the companies evade accountability for their actions.
Instead of OpenAI being prosecuted for creating malware that hacked another company, press releases, news outlets, media personalities, and lawmakers refer to “rogue models” as if they acted on their own. Instead of researchers being questioned about their companies’ habit of plagiarizing academics’ work or using customer data to train models without consent, the public’s imagination is redirected to fears about what the future might hold upon the arrival of fictional superintelligent machines.
The AI industry has even suggested that popular, bipartisan anti-data-center activism is a “distraction” from attempts to regulate the impending, scary, “superhuman” machines these companies are building. According to the AI industry, we should be more worried about a fictional machine god than about the climate catastrophe that these data centers exacerbate, the asthma suffered by those living near them, the rising electricity bills of the public subsidizing them, or the water that is redirected to cooling them.
We know better than to make decisions based on marketing and better than to capitulate to corporate pressure to make those decisions quickly. Wise decision-making, by policymakers and communities, demands time to hear from independent experts and contextualize corporate claims. The best possible outcome from this summer of hype is that policymakers and the public at large learn to take a breath, hold onto our skepticism, and recognize this kind of hype for what it is the next time it comes around.
Timnit Gebru is executive director of DAIR and author of the forthcoming book Deep Unlearning: The Radicalization of a Tech Idealist, which is available for preorders now and set to publish on February 16. Emily M. Bender is professor of linguistics at the University of Washington and coauthor of The AI Con.

articles.title: Reverse-Engineering Flock Cameras - Schneier on Security
articles.text:
Reverse-Engineering Flock Cameras
Hackers captured a Flock camera and got a look (alternate link) at the software:
While much of the automatic license plate reader’s (ALPR) most sensitive storage remained encrypted and inaccessible, the joint analysis of the recovered data shows that software running on the device explicitly detects people as well as vehicles, license plates, and bicycles. The camera can produce dozens of images of a single passing vehicle and, according to several weeks of recovered logs, generated more than a million images. Its computer-vision software also sometimes isolated bumper stickers and other graphics, including, in one case, an American flag patch on a motorcyclist’s saddlebag.
If you’re wondering how the hackers got by disk encryption, one of the unencrypted partitions contained the key for an encrypted partition. That’s pretty bad security engineering.

articles.title: Google's $899 Googlebook is a bet that you'll buy a new laptop for Gemini | TechCrunch
articles.text:
After first unveiling its new AI-powered laptop, dubbed Googlebook, in May, Google on Monday said the new device is now available for preorder for $899.
Meant to offer a step up from traditional Chromebooks, Googlebooks run on Android OS with a desktop version of the Chrome browser and other familiar ChromeOS elements. However, the real pull for the new devices is that they’ll prominently feature Gemini’s latest capabilities in a new format: the laptop.
Google is trying to offer a laptop with unique features like an AI-powered cursor, vibe-coded widgets, and support for AI-enhanced dictation. The latter is a feature called Rambler, which cleans up messy, rambling brain dumps into readable text.
The move is a bet that AI, specifically Google’s Gemini, could be enough of a draw to get people to buy a new laptop that bakes in AI instead of running them via desktop apps you install or access through the browser. In addition, the devices could eventually replace Chromebooks, bringing millions of former Chromebook customers to Gemini AI.
On the Googlebook, Google is trying to reinvent the “point-and-click” experience of desktop computing to now include an AI element: The cursor serves as a conduit to Gemini. The company suggests various ways this could be used, like highlighting content on a web page for Gemini to work with, asking Gemini to see if an email you’ve hovered your cursor over is suspicious, or selecting images and then asking Gemini to visualize them together.
In practice, this feature isn’t very different from Android’s “Circle to Search,” which allows smartphone owners to use gestures like circling, highlighting, or tapping to connect with Google Search, which of course, also includes AI. While it’s a clever way to take advantage of the ways people use their phones, Circle to Search on its own didn’t inspire a mass exodus to Android.
Similarly, Magic Cursor, as the AI pointer is called, won’t likely be a main selling point for the Googlebook, especially now that we have AI agents that can take over your computer and browser to do tasks for you.
Google’s Rambler, however, may be one of the best of the AI features in this upgrade, as it meets a surprisingly useful need. However, this, too, isn’t enough reason to buy a new device, as it feels more like a feature that’s nice to have than a necessity.
Vibe-coding widgets are a minor addition, as well. Other Googlebook features, like Gemini Spark and Gemini Live, also don’t require special, new hardware.
What’s more interesting about the Googlebook is how it’s seemingly part of Google’s longer-term plan to capture a large part of the K-12 market that currently relies on Chromebooks and push them toward the company’s Gemini AI. There are somewhere around 50 million Chromebooks in schools, used by students and educators, Google has said.
In May, the company told TechCrunch that its current Chromebooks would continue to be supported, though many would become eligible to transition to the new Googlebook experience in the future.
The $899 device will include 12 months of Google AI Pro, which gives you 5TB of cloud storage, Gemini Advanced tools, and 3 months of YouTube Premium, Adobe Photoshop, and more. The devices will receive regular updates for up to 10 years, Google said.
Googlebook preorders are open now on the Google Store and at Best Buy and other retailers. Devices will hit shelves on October 4 in the U.S. and on October 5 in Canada, the U.K., Ireland, France, Germany, and Australia.
Flagship devices in the new range are being built by Acer, ASUS, Dell, HP, and Lenovo, with materials like aluminum, magnesium alloy, and carbon fiber. They feature up to 2.8K OLED displays, haptic glass trackpads, and backlit keyboards. Under the hood, they’ll run on processors from Intel and Qualcomm paired with dedicated NPUs. Google says the device will offer up to 14 hours of battery life.

Researchers at the University of Wisconsin–Madison and Marist University published a technical paper titled “Demystifying Gate-Level Localization of RTL Trojans.”
Abstract Excerpt:
“In this work, we show that RTL Trojans exhibit stable structural and signal-flow patterns post-synthesis, enabling effective detection through targeted heuristics rather than generic ML feature learning. We propose LoRD, a lightweight heuristic-based approach that exploits these distinctive subgraph signatures, achieving near-perfect detection and localization on the contest testcases. Com- pared to a transformer-based ML baseline and top five teams, LoRD achieves on-average a score of 2.957 (out of 3) for Trojan- implanted designs without the data and tuning overhead.”

articles.title: Roborock estrena en España sus nuevos robots aspiradores que cambian la forma de limpiar la casa
articles.text:
Roborock quiere que te olvides de la fregona de una vez por todas y para ello ha lanzado una actualización a su línea de robots aspiradores y aspiradoras de mano. A unos meses de presentarlos en IFA 2026, estos dispositivos cubren todo el espectro de la limpieza doméstica, combinando gran potencia de aspiración con tecnologías avanzadas de fregado y un sistema de navegación inteligente para adaptarse a todos los hogares.
Cada modelo resuelve un problema concreto, como los umbrales en las habitaciones, los muebles bajos donde nunca llega la mopa o el pelo de la mascota que se enreda en cualquier cepillo. La alineación está conformada por los nuevos Roborock Saros 20 Flow Complete, Saros 20 Neo y F25 Pro Turbo, que se complementan con el Qrevo 2 Pro. Todos ellos ya están disponibles a partir de hoy en España a través de Amazon y la tienda oficial, y algunos cuentan con un descuento de lanzamiento.
La oferta de Roborock comienza con el Saros 20 Flow Complete, un buque insignia de apenas 8,98 cm de altura que se ubica como el robot con mopa de rodillo más plano que ha sacado la marca hasta ahora. Esta delgadez le permite colarse bajo muebles y lugares donde otros robots no pueden pasar. A esto se suma un sistema de navegación AdaptiLift Traverse 3.0, el cual añade la capacidad de superar desniveles de hasta 8,8 centímetros en casas con puertas elevadas o cambios de suelo.
Saros 20 Flow Complete, máximo rendimiento
En términos de rendimiento, el Saros 20 Flow Complete cuenta con un potente motor HyperForce que ofrece 36.000 Pa de succión. El robot puede aspirar desde polvo fino hasta restos más voluminosos y cuenta con un doble sistema antienredos para pelo de mascota.
La mopa de rodillo SpiraFlow 2.0 combina 15 N de presión hacia abajo con una rotación de 240 revoluciones por minuto y 16 salidas de agua a presión. Lo anterior se traduce en manchas resecas que desaparecen con una pasada, mientras que los cepillos laterales dobles con elevación en arco completan el barrido de bordes. Para moverse, el robot se apoya en un LDS elevado con escaneo de 360º que se retrae cuando el robot necesita colarse en espacios reducidos.
Toda la parte de mantenimiento del Saros 20 Flow Complete queda en manos de la base RockDock, que lava la mopa con agua a 100 grados y dosifica el detergente automáticamente.
Saros 20 Neo, esbelto, potente y con buena autonomía
Mientras que el modelo Flow Complete apuesta por el pulido, el Saros 20 Neo se enfoca en limpiar todos los rincones con la menor intervención posible. Este modelo es todavía más esbelto que su hermano mayor, ya que cuenta con una altura de acceso de apenas 7,95 cm que se combina con un chasis AdaptiLift 3.0 para salvar umbrales de doble capa de hasta 8,8 cm.
El Saros 20 Neo ofrece el mismo motor que el Flow Complete, con 36.000 Pa de succión y doble sistema antienredos. Donde encontramos cambios es en la gestión de obstáculos, ya que este modelo se apoya en un sistema impulsado por IA que es capaz de reconocer más de 300 objetos distintos, esquivar cables sueltos y limpiar detrás de las cortinas.
En la parte de fregado, el Saros 20 Neo usa agua caliente y hasta 14 N de presión para deshacerse de la suciedad. El robot también usa IA para detectar automáticamente los tipos de manchas y ajustar la potencia para aquellas que sean más complejas de limpiar. Para aquellos que tienen alfombras, hay una función pensada para evitar que se mojen en exceso, aunque deberá activarse desde la aplicación móvil.
El punto fuerte de este modelo es la batería, que según Roborock, le permite limpiar hasta 350 metros cuadrados sin interrupciones. El Neo incluye una base multifuncional que se encarga del llenado automático de agua tibia y ajusta la intensidad de limpieza según la suciedad.
F25 Pro Turbo, para quienes no quieren un robot
Acompañando a la familia de robots, Roborock lanzó la F25 Pro Turbo, una aspiradora en seco y húmedo pensada para limpiar manchas puntuales. Este dispositivo ofrece una potencia de aspiración de hasta 25.000 Pa y una tecnología HyperScrub que aumenta el flujo del agua y la velocidad del rodillo a través de un gatillo ubicado en el mango.
En cuanto a funciones, la F25 Pro Turbo integra un sistema de doble raspador JawScrapers que evita que el pelo se enrede en el rodillo. El diseño FlatReach 2.0 permite reclinar el cuerpo 180 grados hasta los 12,5 centímetros de altura, una distancia que le ayuda a entrar bajo el sofá o la cama sin que la succión se resienta. Este manejo se apoya en las ruedas del sistema SlideTech 2.0, que ayudan a empujar y girar el aparato casi sin esfuerzo.
Al igual que los robots aspiradores, el Roborock F25 Pro Turbo tiene una base con mantenimiento automático que se autolava a 95 grados y seca el rodillo en cinco minutos. La batería ofrece hasta una hora de autonomía, que sería suficiente para cubrir un área de hasta 460 metros cuadrados con una sola carga.
Precio y disponibilidad de los nuevos aspiradores de Roborock
- El Saros 20 Flow Complete ya está disponible en España por 1.299 euros en Amazon y en la web oficial de Roborock.
- El Saros 20 Neo puede encontrarse por 999 euros, también en Amazon y en la tienda oficial de la marca.
- El Qrevo 2 Pro ya está disponible en España a un precio de 689 euros en Amazon, El Corte Inglés, PcComponentes y en la web oficial de Roborock.
- El F25 Pro Turbo tiene un precio oficial de 549 euros, aunque durante el Prime Day, del 29 de septiembre al 8 de octubre, bajará hasta los 449 euros, disponible igualmente en Amazon y en la web de Roborock.

articles.title: Why Nigeria’s FriendnPal is building an AI-powered mobile therapy service - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Nigerian startup FriendnPal is building an AI-powered behavioural health intelligence and remote patient monitoring platform designed to detect mental health risks earlier, close treatment gaps, intervene sooner, and deliver continuous care at scale.
Founded in 2023 by Esther Eruchie, following a deeply personal experience with mental health and the loss of her mother to depression, FriendnPal combines multimodal AI, behavioural analytics, digital phenotyping, clinical assessments, risk stratification, remote patient monitoring and human clinical triage to detect changes in behavioural and psychological patterns over time.
“Globally, mental healthcare is largely reactive, a person becomes symptomatic, seeks help, receives an assessment and is eventually connected to care, but FriendnPal is building the infrastructure to make care continuous, predictive and preventive,” Eruchie told Disrupt Africa.
FriendnPal does not position its AI as a replacement for clinicians, but rather a tool for them to use to better serve patients.
“Our AI identifies patterns and risk signals, where risk is detected, users can be triaged to licensed mental health professionals, creating a human-in-the-loop model of care. Our platform is designed for emerging markets, where affordability, language, geography and connectivity remain significant barriers,” Eruchie said.
The platform, which is accessible through mobile, web, voice and WhatsApp, and supports over 50 languages, has moved from primarily direct-to-consumer mental health support towards a broader B2B/B2B2C behavioural health infrastructure model, working with healthcare providers, enterprises, institutions, governments and research organisations.
Most healthcare systems only see a patient’s mental health at isolated points: during an appointment, screening or crisis,” said Eruchie.
“But deterioration happens between those moments. FriendnPal captures longitudinal behavioural signals and combines them with clinical assessments and contextual information to create a more continuous picture of an individual’s wellbeing.”
This enables a shift from reactive to predictive, crisis intervention to early intervention, and periodic assessment to continuous monitoring.
“We believe this creates a significant opportunity as healthcare moves toward preventive, personalised and digitally enabled models of care,” said Eruchie.
“We are not simply building another chatbot or therapy marketplace, we are building infrastructure that can sit between individuals and healthcare systems to identify changing risk and support earlier intervention.”
FriendnPal, thus far self-funded, has already reached almost 90,000 people, and completed over 60,000 behavioural and clinical assessments. Within that, almost 1,500 “suicide-risk cases” were intercepted and supported through intervention pathways, demonstrating the startup’s impact. In doing so, it has also generated over US$100,000 in revenues.
“Uptake has grown from direct consumer adoption into institutional and international demand. Our early traction validated that people are willing to use digital channels for mental health support, particularly where traditional services are inaccessible or unaffordable. Our subsequent focus has been on proving that the underlying behavioural intelligence infrastructure can generate value for organisations,” Eruchie said.
“We are increasingly seeing demand from healthcare providers, employers, universities, governments, research institutions and international organisations interested in earlier identification, remote monitoring, triage and scalable behavioural health support. We currently have users across Nigeria, South Africa, Kenya, Japan, Germany, the US and the UK, and are now moving into a more deliberate international expansion phase, particularly in Europe.”
The startup, which also plans to deepen its presence across African markets, operates a freemium and B2B/B2C model.
“For individuals, we generate revenue primarily through paid therapy sessions, subscriptions, therapy packages and premium mental health services,” said Eruchie.
“For organisations and institutions, we provide structured mental health and wellbeing solutions, including employee assistance programmes, institutional deployments and partnerships that provide mental health support to employees, beneficiaries, founders or communities. We also generate recurring revenue through, implementation fees, API licensing, remote patient monitoring solutions, and behavioral analytics.”

articles.title: Open-source is more than free code. It’s a way to build for the future
articles.text:
Open-source is more than free code. It’s a way to build for the future
From sovereign AI to open-code culture, Margaret Dawson on what it really takes to build for the AI era.
What does open-source really mean when artificial intelligence is changing how companies build, scale, and innovate? For SUSE CMO Margaret Dawson, it goes far beyond free software. In a conversation with YourStory, she explores why Indian startups need to think about open-source as a strategic advantage.
Be it building sovereign AI architectures and avoiding vendor lock-in or creating workplaces where ideas matter more than hierarchy, Dawson explores how open-source could be key to building AI-ready organisations.
Edited excerpts:
YS: When founders hear “open-source”, many immediately think of free tools or licenses. How would you reframe it for the AI era, and why should Indian startups care beyond cost savings?
MD: In the AI era, treating open-source as a discount code is a massive strategic mistake. Open-source isn't just a license; it is a development model, a technology process, and an architectural strategy based on control, choice, and speed.
For Indian startups scaling at breakneck speed, open-source is about avoiding the 10x architectural tax down the road. It gives you the composable foundation to ensure interoperability across multi-cloud and edge environments, fine-tune models on your own IP, and innovate without permission or lock-in.
When model pricing shifts, APIs get deprecated, or data governance mandates evolve, open-source keeps you in the driver’s seat of your own business. Also, it ensures your developers are working in the technologies they love or want to learn, and you have the option to purchase the supported, enterprise-ready version of that software.
YS: You’ve been driving SUSE’s Sovereign AI strategy. For a CTO in Bengaluru or Hyderabad, what does “Sovereign AI” look like in practice, and where are you seeing Indian companies start?
MD: There is a misconception that digital sovereignty is a uniquely European compliance headache. That’s simply not true — sovereignty is a global operational imperative.
For a CTO in Bengaluru or Hyderabad, it comes down to three non-negotiable capabilities:
- Control over data and model lineage: Knowing exactly where your data, prompt context, and model weights reside.
- Supply chain transparency: Complete visibility into every layer of the software stack, from the Linux kernel and container runtime up to the LLM orchestration layer.
- Operational autonomy: The freedom to run workloads air-gapped, on-premises, or across hybrid clouds without a mandatory umbilical cord to a single cloud provider.
Deloitte research indicates that 65% of organizations have abandoned AI initiatives midway, primarily due to skills gaps, data residency risks, and infrastructure lock-in. Our own research validates this. Indian tech leaders are starting where the risk is highest: regulated enterprise workloads and fine-tuning open-weight models on private data. They are abandoning the "public-cloud-first" of the past in favor of hybrid, governed architectures. You cannot build a sovereign future inside a black box; transparency and open standards are the only way to guarantee true control.
YS: The core idea here is adopting open-source ways of working internally — transparency, meritocracy of ideas, psychological safety. Can you share one example where an “InnerSourcing” or open-community practice inside a company broke silos and sped up delivery?
MD: As I shared in my SUSECON keynote on the Power of Open, true openness isn't just about software licenses, but rather it rests on three interconnected pillars: Open Standards, Open Architecture, and Open Culture. You simply cannot build an open, sovereign AI future if your leadership operates with a closed, command-and-control mindset. In an open-source culture, the best ideas win regardless of title, and contribution always trumps hierarchy.
InnerSourcing changes the entire operating model by applying open-source community principles inside the company. A clear example of this in action was how we transformed our cross-functional go-to-market campaigns and AI agent workflow architecture across marketing, sales, support, and our products.
Our agentic ecosystem, fully aligned to our brand style and voice, now guides prospects and customers through their discovery journey, appointment setting, sales and support questions, and technical implementation.
YS: A lot of older Indian tech firms talk about innovation but run on closed, hierarchy-heavy management. What are some specific management behaviors or rituals that demonstrate a team is truly embodying an open-source culture, not just using the label?
MD: If you want to know whether an organization genuinely lives an open-source culture, look at their daily operational habits:
- Working in the open: Information is treated as a collaboration opportunity, with strategy, roadmaps, decisions, and learnings openly documented across the company.
- Blameless learning: When things go wrong, leaders focus on systemic bottlenecks rather than blame, making workflows more inspectable and repeatable.
- Prototypes over titles: Ideas are judged by data, logic and working code, not seniority. A working prototype from a junior engineer beats a 50-slide deck from a Vice President every single time.
YS: In open-source communities, contribution trumps pedigree. How can Indian startups create hiring, promotion, and project governance so that self-taught engineers, women in tech, and career-switchers can thrive — not just be “included”?
MD: I care deeply about this topic because talent shortages or skill sets remain the single largest bottleneck to AI adoption. IDC projects that 90% of enterprises will face critical AI skills shortages by 2026, representing an estimated $5.5 trillion in unrealized productivity globally. You simply cannot solve a talent shortage of that scale using legacy, pedigree-heavy hiring filters.
In open-source communities, no one asks where you went to school; they look at your pull requests, your problem-solving logic, and your passion. Startups can replicate this through three deliberate shifts:
- Skills-based hiring: Replace pedigree-heavy screening with problem-solving challenges and reviews of relevant work or open-source contributions.
- Transparent growth paths: Clearly define the objective milestones required to earn leadership or maintainer roles.
- Reciprocal mentorship: Pair non-traditional talent with senior leaders, creating two-way learning—junior employees share AI-native skills while leaders offer strategic and executive guidance.
When people feel safe to bring their curiosity and "work out loud,” style, diversity stops being a corporate compliance metric and becomes your ultimate innovation engine.
YS: Skill gaps are repeatedly cited as the primary obstacle to AI adoption. Instead of “train everyone on LLMs,” what open-source-style learning models (peer review, community docs, contributor ladders) have you seen actually move the needle on upskilling teams for AI work?
MD: Pushing top-down, passive video training modules on a team rarely builds real operational capability. Organizations that establish structured, hands-on learning achieve a 3.7x to 10.3x average return on their AI investments.
The biggest need I see here is to recognize how everyone learns and retains information differently. You need to have training content that is watched, listened to, read, and experienced.
Active, community-driven models work best for upskilling: peer-review prompts and agent workflows, use sandboxes and hackathons to build real-world prototypes, and replace static training with living, community-driven documentation. Make learning collaborative, even for non-technical teams, and recognise cross-functional wins — not just individual technical expertise. Programmes such as “AI Stars of the Week” can celebrate teams that use AI together to innovate, solve problems and move the business forward.
YS: For a founder reading this who wants to start leveraging open-source culture tomorrow, what’s the smallest, high-impact change they could make in the next 30 days?
MD: Open up one key strategic discussion currently happening behind closed doors. Choose a product pivot, architectural decision, or operational bottleneck, and publish the context, constraints, and data internally.
Then host an open, cross-functional working session with developers, marketers, product managers, and customer leads. Ask: “What are we missing?” and “How do we unblock this together?” When leaders show that clarity and good ideas matter more than hierarchy, they’re building a culture of openness.

articles.title: Grâce à cette ruse d'Apple, plus de smartphones Android vont pouvoir gagner en autonomie
articles.text:
Les capacités des batteries de certains smartphones grimpent en flèche depuis quelques années, mais les réglementations internationales imposent une contrainte logistique importante : en Europe comme aux États-Unis, les réseaux de transport limitent une cellule de batterie unique à 20 Wh. Pour contourner cela, certains smartphones utilisent des batteries plus petites ou des architectures à deux batteries, ce qui n’est pas le cas de l’iPhone 18 Pro Max, qui a une seule batterie de 5 391 mAh. Apple utilise en effet un bridage par micrologiciel afin de respecter ces normes aériennes et routières, sans pour autant sacrifier l’autonomie. Explications.
Une limitation activée de l’usine jusqu’au déballage du téléphone
Pendant la phase de fabrication et tout au long du transport depuis l’usine, le système limite la capacité de l’accumulateur sous la barre des 20 Wh. Dès que l’utilisateur déballe son iPhone 18 Pro Max et procède à sa configuration, la restriction logicielle disparaît pour libérer l’intégralité de la charge disponible.
Les appareils stockés dans leur boîte d’origine intègrent déjà cette protection temporaire qui ne demande aucune manipulation de la part des utilisateurs. C’est une méthode assez astucieuse qui pourrait éviter aux fabricants de smartphones de multiplier les architectures à double batterie pour se conformer aux réglementations d’acheminement sur certains continents, comme en Europe et aux États-Unis.
Une fonction dédiée pour expédier son appareil en toute sécurité
Apple a aussi pensé au fait que l’utilisateur peut vouloir renvoyer son téléphone pour une réparation, une reprise, un retour ou un cadeau par exemple. Dans ce cas, il doit activer manuellement une option spécifique dans les menus. En passant par les paramètres de réinitialisation, la fonction « Préparer pour l’expédition » décharge l’accumulateur sous le seuil réglementaire et fixe une limite de charge temporaire. Apple précise que l’iPhone 18 Pro Max peut avoir besoin de se décharger pour se préparer à l’expédition et que le téléphone peut « chauffer plus que d’habitude » à ce moment précis, mais qu’il refroidira lorsqu’il sera prêt à être expédié. Une fois le processus mené à son terme, l’interface affiche le statut « Prêt à l’expédition » pour attester que le colis respecte les exigences de transport.
La batterie du smartphone sera alors limitée à 80 % pendant 14 jours. Passé ce délai, il sera possible de désactiver la fonction « Préparer pour l’expédition » afin de retrouver la pleine capacité de la batterie de l’appareil. Malin, non ?

articles.title: Tom Cruise y Emily Blunt presentaron en 24 horas y en dos continentes una de las mejores pelis de ciencia ficción de los últimos 15 años
articles.text:
Tom Cruise es conocido por sus hazañas atrevidas y dignas de récord, casi siempre en forma de acrobacias temerarias de esas que quitan el hipo. Pero con 'Al filo del mañana' se sacó de la manga un plan de locos digno de 'Misión Imposible', solo que de otro tipo: tres estrenos, en dos continentes y en apenas 24 horas. Ni uno ni dos: tres, y con el cronómetro en marcha.
La secuela, cada vez más cerca. Una vez más, se han multiplicado los indicios de que pronto arrancará el rodaje de la esperada secuela de 'Edge of Tomorrow', que aquí en España conocemos como 'Al filo del mañana'. Hay que decir que tiene todo el sentido del mundo, porque después del estreno en cines de esta peli de bucles temporales allá por 2014, los fans pedían a gritos una segunda parte.
Un éxito con crítica y taquilla. El filme fue una de esas rarezas que pegan el pelotazo en la taquilla y, al mismo tiempo, dejan tan contento al público como a la prensa especializada. La web estadounidense Rotten Tomatoes recoge un 91% de críticas positivas, mientras que los usuarios también se rinden con un 90% de aprobación. Y el que escribe lo secunda.
Blunt, a ciegas hasta el final. Visto lo visto, cuesta creer que la protagonista, Emily Blunt, se fuera poniendo cada vez más nerviosa según se acercaba el estreno del film de acción y ciencia ficción dirigido por Doug Liman ('Mr. & Mrs. Smith'). Y es que durante mucho tiempo no tuvo ni idea de qué se traía entre manos el equipo de marketing, ni de dónde se iba a proyectar siquiera la película.
Un estreno era poco para Cruise. Lo que ella no sabía es que su compañero de reparto llevaba tiempo con una idea en la cabeza y, como corresponde a la estrella de 'Misión: Imposible' y su afición a las acrobacias, no una cualquiera. No planeaba un estreno, sino tres, en tres ciudades distintas de dos continentes y en 24 horas. "Cuando me enteré de que habría tres estrenos, simplemente dije: 'Esto es una idea de Tom Cruise'", contó la actriz en una entrevista recogida por Sensacine.
Londres, París y Nueva York. Como es imposible celebrar de noche tres estrenos tan alejados entre sí, y con todos los implicados presentes, el maratón arrancó a las 6:30 de la mañana en Londres. Al mediodía llegó el segundo pase en París, antes de que la gira relámpago pusiera su punto final por la noche en Nueva York. ¿Se arrepintió Cruise de su plan descabellado, aunque fuera un poco, después del último vuelo? Por supuesto que no. Y eso que había tomado sus precauciones para que el viaje fuera lo más cómodo posible para el reparto y el equipo.
Un vuelo entero en pijama. En el primer trayecto, Cruise y Blunt coincidieron con el resto del reparto y con el director Doug Liman en el mismo avión, una experiencia que ambos describieron como "muy divertida". El segundo vuelo, el transatlántico, fue algo distinto: esta vez los dos actores viajaron solos en su propio jet, donde pudieron descansar. Según Blunt, ella se pasó toda la travesía en pijama.
"Es como rodar una película". Cruise también echó una cabezada, aunque breve. "Me siento bien, es como rodar una película. Duermes un par de horas, te levantas y sigues", aseguró el hoy actor de 63 años. En el estreno de Nueva York se tomó una hora entera para hacerse fotos con los fans en la alfombra roja.

articles.title: Opening TeraBox Video Links Through Telegram: What Android Users Should Check - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Android users may sometimes receive TeraBox video links through chats, forums, or social groups and find that opening or playing the content is less straightforward than expected.
Some users may consider Telegram bots that claim to process TeraBox links and return a playable video, a download option, or another form of file response.
These bots should be approached with caution. TeraBox-related Telegram bots are third-party services, not official TeraBox features. Their availability, functionality, and reliability can change without notice.
Why People Use Telegram Bots for TeraBox Links
A shared TeraBox URL may lead to a video stored on TeraBox, but access depends on factors such as the file owner’s sharing settings, the type of link, account requirements, and the device being used.
A Telegram bot may provide another way to process a shared link. Depending on the individual bot, it may return a preview, a playable link, a download option, or no usable result at all. Users should therefore check the bot’s current instructions and supported link types rather than assuming that every bot works in the same way.
How Android Users Can Try a TeraBox Link-Processing Bot
The exact commands and available features vary between bots. If a user chooses to try one, the general process may be:
- Find a relevant Telegram bot. Search Telegram for a TeraBox link-processing bot and review its description and instructions. MiniTelegram’s TeraBox bot listing is an independent directory listing; MiniTelegram does not operate the bot listed there.
- Check the bot before sharing a link. Confirm that it is currently available and responding and that it clearly states which TeraBox links it supports. Avoid bots or linked pages that request unnecessary passwords, account credentials, or access permissions.
- Open the bot. From Telegram, open the bot and tap Start if that option is shown, or follow the instructions provided in the chat.
- Copy an authorized TeraBox share link. On Android, copy the TeraBox URL you have permission to access and share. You do not need to make a private file public simply to use a bot.
- Submit the link if the bot supports it. Paste the authorized share link into the bot and follow its current instructions. Depending on the service, the response may be a preview, another link, a downloadable file, or no result.
- Check the bot’s response and any linked destination. Before opening an external page or downloading anything, check where it leads and whether the result appears consistent with the original content.
Checklist Before Using a TeraBox Telegram Bot
Before submitting a link, check:
- Current availability: Is the bot currently available and responding?
- Supported links: Does it clearly state which TeraBox link formats or files it supports?
- Credentials and access: Does it request passwords, account credentials, or permissions that are not necessary?
- File source and permissions: Do you trust the source of the TeraBox file, and are you authorized to access or share it?
- Third-party sharing: Are you comfortable sending the TeraBox URL to a third-party service?
What to Keep in Mind
Third-party bots can stop working, change their features, impose usage limits, or provide different types of output over time. Availability and results can vary, so users should rely on the bot’s current instructions rather than assuming that a particular feature is guaranteed.
Privacy is another important consideration. Sending a TeraBox URL to a third-party bot means that the URL is being provided to a service outside TeraBox and Telegram. Avoid sharing sensitive or private links unless you understand the associated risks.
Finally, using a bot does not change ownership or permissions associated with a file. Only access or share TeraBox content that you are authorized to use, and do not use third-party tools to bypass access restrictions.
Telegram bots may be useful for some authorized TeraBox links, but they are not a guaranteed or official TeraBox solution. Checking current bot functionality, link requirements, permissions, and privacy considerations can help Android users make a more informed decision before submitting a link.

articles.title: WordPress Click2Shell flaw lets hackers execute PHP on the server
articles.text:
Technical details and a proof-of-concept exploit have been published for a new WordPress cross-site request forgery (CSRF) vulnerability dubbed 'Click2Shell' that affects the platform’s Core component.
The security problem does not have an official identifier but was addressed last week with the release of WordPress version 7.1.1.
It is a pre-authenticated remote code execution chain that allows an attacker to install any theme in the official WordPress.org catalog and run an arbitrary PHP file.
Security researcher Paulos Yibelo of the autonomous penetration testing platform pwn.ai discovered Click2Shell and reported it to WordPress on August 22.
The researchers explain that "a value from a WordPress theme-preview URL is interpreted once by the WordPress.org Themes API and a second, buggy methods by JavaScript in the Administrator's browser."
This enables an attacker to add a WordPress theme to a target website without the administrator explicitly installing it. The researcher found that even if inactive, a theme could still execute PHP during a Customizer preview.
It should be noted that even if the attacker does not need to authenticate, a logged-in administrator needs to visit a crafted URL for the Click2Shell exploit to work.
An attack could start with a crafted link that leads to installing a vulnerable theme in the catalog. Once the Customizer preview loads the inactive theme's PHP, the code is executed on the server.
To demonstrate the issue, pwn.ai used a vulnerable WordPress theme as the second component in the chain that executed the attacker's PHP code.
The researcher's full technical report provides a complete proof-of-concept (PoC) exploit for achieving server-side remote code execution.
Executing code this way could enable file modification and deletion, access to user data, and the ‘wp-config.php’ file that contains database credentials and authentication secrets. An attacker could leverage this access to create rogue admin accounts or inject malicious scripts.
Although Yibelo demonstrated Click2Shell using a particular theme, the underlying flaw in WordPress Core 7.1.0 and earlier could be leveraged to force-install any other vulnerable theme in the WordPress catalog.
The researcher notes that an attacker does not need a WordPress account, an installation nonce, or their own administrative privileges. However, a Click2Shell attack requires a logged-in administrator to visit the crafted link.
WordPress security firm Patchstack analyzed Click2Shell and highlights that only an administrator can trigger the chain, while Author and Editor accounts lack the required permission to install themes.
The company warned that attacks are possible via targeted phishing or an existing cross-site scripting (XSS) flaw that makes the administrator’s browser send the request.
WordPress fixed the Core vulnerability in version 7.1.1 by escaping the theme slug before using it in the jQuery selector and restricting the selector to actual theme cards.
For administrators who cannot install the update immediately, Patchstack says that websites with ‘DISALLOW_FILE_MODS’ enabled cannot be forced to install the theme or a malicious plugin.
However, switching to the latest WordPress version is a strong recommendation, especially with complete technical details and a PoC already public.
